action_text:
Edward Fontanin, Utility Services Director, stated this is legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance to sunset the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District on December 31, 2029; the background behind this, the last bond payment for Barefoot Bay is December 2029; in December 2029 there will be no debt service associated with the District and as a result while currently working on the replacement of the water and wastewater plant of Barefoot Bay, that will actually be outside of the District; compound that with the fact that the legislature of the mandate related to discharges and the integrity of pipes and whatnot; it also gets restrictive in the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District because it is a dependent district which means they can only spend what they generate within that district; and the way staff sees it is debt service at the 2029 will be paid off, it will be transferred over to the Countywide system, which is still currently operating, and it will give staff more freedom to transfer money for expenditures that are needed within the district without the financial confines of the dependent district.
Sydne James stated the information she has provided the Board is a good faith estimate of accurate data that she was able to research; she has focused in her document on base wastewater rates because Barefoot Bay water rates are similar to other communities, but the wastewater rates are not; the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer system was purchased in 2000 from the Florida Governmental Utility Authority; the residential customers who are serviced by it are the only customers in unincorporated Brevard County who pay for their own specific water treatment plant; it is neither fair nor equitable; the base wastewater rate for approximately 5,000 Barefoot Bay customers is currently $54.28, and for the other 69,400 residential customers in unincorporated Brevard County it is $28.17; and the Agenda Item tonight is to integrate into the Countywide system on December 31, 2029, after the current debt obligation is fulfilled, the question of when to make this happen, integrating them, should not be about current Barefoot Bay debt, it should be about deciding when to eliminate the inequity, the disparity, the unfairness, call it whatever, it is all of these things that the Barefoot Bay water and sewer plant have to be burdened by only 5,000 residents when the other five plants serviced by 69,400 residential customers get to divide that up amongst so many more people. She went on to say the roll back to 2025 rates indicate in the press release that it amounts to a decrease of only $2.66 per month on sewer rates; it is too small of an amount to have any meaningful relief; if Barefoot Bay was immediately integrated into the Countywide system, the customers, everybody else except Barefoot Bay, base sewer rates would increase by approximately $1.58 per month, not even noticeable, but Barefoot bay would decrease from $54.28 or the proposed lower rate of $51.62 to only $29.75; this decrease would make a profound impact to the lives of many customers in Barefoot Bay, especially those who only live on Social Security income and are struggling to get by; the residents are not asking for a handout, or special treatment, all they are asking is for the Board to remove the yoke tying them to the Barefoot Bay District and to be treated like all the other residential customers in unincorporated Brevard County; many cannot bear the heavy weight of this yoke for three and one-half more years; and she asked the Board to please do it now or at the very latest December 31, 2026.
John Requa stated he has been to the Board twice and said the same thing, but Ms. James said it more eloquently; he has spoken to the Director before and sent him by registered mail, four questions that he never got answers to; he noted the questions were what was the price of the bond when he started, how much has been paid in, how much do the residents own, and did they receive the upgrades that he told were part of the deal with the bond; he would really like to have those questions answered; the other thing is for Commissioner Adkinson to hold true to what she said in the Tatler of October 2025, the cost of the bond should be spread across the District; they are District 3, Barefoot Bay does not own that facility, they do not run that facility, the County does; that is what they are asking and that is what legal counsel has asked her from Barefoot Bay; and that is all the residents want. He went on to say people are suffering under these fees, and people are leaving; the price of water, homeowners of modular homes, taxes, the Board is going to turn Palm Bay into a trailer park and then maybe Ashton Park to take it over; that is how bad the residents are hurt; he hopes the Board listens to him and responds; Ms. James is absolutely correct in saying to spread the cost of the bond over the District, that is all the residents want; he does not have any hope in a new plant or in that reducing the prices because he does not believe it one bit; and he has no reason to see any good merit that is going to come when the Board will not listen to the people and will not act on their pleas. He noted he will surrender the rest of his time as he has said twice before.
Adriane Pearl stated she lives in Barefoot Bay and she would like to address the monthly rising cost of the water bills; she believes they are being estimated; there have been several customers getting $200 and $300 bills that are older couples; they do not understand why their bills are so high, they go to the water company and are told they have leaks; they gets plumbers to come out and there are no leaks; she is on Social Security Disability and lives on $1,400 per month which is not easy especially with the rising cost of insurance; she has the same routine every month, she does not do anything differently, and she is a one-person household; residents are being told that there is one meter reader for approximately 5,000 homes in their District; and there is no way one person, even with the new digital meters can get to 5,000 homes to read these meters. She noted she has three bills here, May, June, and July; May and June were $92.59, the exact same amount and the exact same water usage; she finds that to be physically impossible, one cannot use the exact same amount every month for two months in a row; in July, her bill jumped from $92.59 to $100.08; what she has found is happening is every two months she is receiving duplicate bills and the third month it is arbitrarily raised anywhere from $8 to $10 a month; when she first moved to Barefoot Bay her bill was $50, and now she is looking at over $100; she is literally drowning, she cannot afford it any longer; and she is asking the Board to address this community and try to do what the customers are asking it to do if at all possible because they cannot afford $200 to $300 water bills. She mentioned as of next year, this is totally not within the scope here, but as of next year with the insurance crisis because everyone is under Citizens Property Insurance Corporation, she is probably going to lose her home as she is paying $4,000 right now; next year they are going to have the flood assessment even though she is not in a flood district; these bills are getting astronomical and ludicrous; something has to be done; there are a lot of lower income families there and she would like for Commissioner Adkinson, if possible, to address the fact of how many exact employees are reading the meters; one of the ladies told them that they were short staffed and they did not know what to tell people; and she would appreciate that.
Sandra Sullivan stated one of the things Commissioner Delaney brought to this Board, which she really appreciated, was her transparency; when it comes to this, District 3 is in the process, and was just approved buying a parcel next to this facility to presumably put in a toilet to tap, sewage to drinking water facility; that was estimated to be $319 million if she recalls correctly from last year; when she looked legislatively what counties are asking for, what she did not see for Brevard is any appropriation requests to any of the State Representatives for that; obviously, if the burden keeps being placed on the people, because to their point, Barefoot Bay, when the people had the increases, hers was 46 percent over five years, she did not calculate Barefoot Bay’s, theirs was way more; they were like over 10 percent a year increases; and she asked if the rest of the County, for sewage and the water systems, at the same rate. She continued to say the County has certain plants that are in worse condition, sewage plants on that side, that is not sewage it is water, but even up in Titusville the water plant, there was something on the Agenda to night; there are issues with plants, water, sewage, and different areas of critical needs to be addressed; she asked to that point is there validity, it is just a thought to have everybody on the same rate for equity; she mentioned the County manages things; it took it over; she remembers the vote when the County took over that facility as Special District; it does not need to be a Special District waiting until 2029; and she asked if there is a way to get out of that earlier. She mentioned she questions more than anything, given the comments that have been made because it is a very high rate compared to what everybody else has; she would like to see some transparency regarding the County’s plans for funding the new facility because this Agenda Item says this plan is at the end of its life; it cannot be recouped and kept going, it is end of life; and she inquired what is the replacement plan, how does the County plan to fund it, and what is going to be done to try to mitigate that so it does not all end up on the people.
Rick Heffelfinger stated this is Utility Services Department again; this whole water situation, he has never been able to understand how many water plants, who pays for them, how people are rate increased, and how they are not; he does not know who controls this one; it sounds like the Barefoot Bay facility is part of the big Brevard system, but they are obviously charging different fees; now it turns out the County is going to sunset them after they pay off their debt, but they are going to collect fees from now until then; he would guess they have not been saving anything for a plant because the plant is shot; he asked if there is a fund that accumulated money so they can give it to Brevard County so that it can work on that other plant; and he commented he does not know what that other plant is. He asked why not shut this plant down run a pipe to the new plant and just put that one over capacity as well; he mentioned he does not know if this one is over capacity; he inquired if it is still one million gallons per day or if it has been upgraded from that; he commented he does not know; the chart on the County page, he already knows it is out-of-date because it says they were going to have the South/Central Park completed in 2019; well it was, it is at $12 million so this has not been updated, therefore, he cannot use the County web page to figure anything out; when he tries to figure out what is going on, but he did pull these service billing rates, and this is the most convoluted thing; he even tried to figure out what zone and area that he is in and there is no connection fee or anything; he does not know if anybody is building a new place in Barefoot Bay; and he asked if they are going to get those connection fees as well. He inquired if there are any empty properties in there; he stated the County could get some serious cash just by nailing them with those connection fees right there; that might go into the coffers; he does not know why the Board is waiting to pay off debt as they are collecting services and not placing any of that service fee money into an account because they have not maintained it, the plant is dead, it is way past use, and nothing was reinvested; and he asked if that was staffs job to reinvest, or the Board’s job to reinvest. He stated he does not know what they did if they just stood around and managed it; and the water system here sucks.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she has a couple questions; she understands that the new plant down there is going to service Barefoot Bay, Snug Harbor, and the rest of the residents who need servicing; and she asked if Mr. Fontanin can tell her what the total debt is for Barefoot Bay, currently.
Mr. Fontanin replied he believes it is somewhere around $4 million, but he will have to double check that.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if Mr. Fontanin can tell her very briefly how that debt occurred.
Mr. Fontanin explained that Barefoot Bay from its existence was operated as a development with their own private water sewer system; he thinks late '60s or early '70s where this occurred, as they grew, his understanding is around mid to late '90s, the people of Barefoot Bay were complaining of the service that the private utility was providing them; based on that, and he does not know much detail, it made it to the Board and the Board in '97 or '99 agreed to bring Barefoot Bay as part of the County system on the condition that it be done as a Dependent District; why it was decided to do it as a Dependent District, he does not have the background; and however, he thinks there was discussion that there was fear back in '93 that the people of Barefoot Bay were concerned that the revenue generated there would go to other areas.
Commissioner Adkinson remarked that is how the debt happened and that is how it was incurred.
Mr. Fontanin stated in order for the County to get ownership of the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District, there was an amount that had to be paid to that entity of $25 or $30 million in order for that transaction to occur.
Commissioner Adkinson stated clearly she has heard tonight that people would like to just be on the County system because they feel that it will be better; her question would be can Mr. Fontanin sit down with her behind closed doors and help her to concoct an argument that she can give to the rest of the Board, how to convince them that all of the other residents in Brevard County should take on this debt; and she asked if Mr. Fontanin could help her with that argument.
Mr. Fontanin advised he thinks that is more of a legal question about how user rates in the Countywide system can be used in that regard; and he can have a further conversation with her.
Commissioner Adkinson stated maybe that is a County Attorney, Morris Richardson, question if it is about legality; and she apologized for placing attorney Richardson on the spot.
Attorney Richardson stated he thinks she is absolutely right about the discussion that happened back then; it was viewed by the County Commission and County residents as a bailout of this private system, so they did not want to wall it off; they created that District, but because of the bond issue, the revenue bonds do not constitute a debt liability or obligation of the County, they are an obligation of being paid solely from the revenues that are generated from the District; and that is part of the reason that even if the Board were inclined to forget the history and the bailout, try to rest and make things on equal standing. He noted they cannot use revenue from other parts of the County system to pay off those bonds; those bonds have to be payable and secured; the rates have to be sufficient; it violates the bond covenants if the rate were not set at a sufficient amount to service that debt; that is why Mr. Fontanin had to do the study; while he was trying to get them some relief, the study sets the parameters of what relief it can afford, but still generate enough revenue to be able to satisfy and service that bond; now, fortunately they are very close to the end of that road; it has been a long time when that was established, 1999; and it will be 30 years in 2029. He mentioned that by providing an ordinance that sunsets the District now and then following up with a rate resolution that affords whatever relief that it can, which is rolling back the rates somewhat, but also freezing those rates at that rolled back rate so they do not continue to escalate every year; and there will come a point when its sunset where it will be rolled in with a new plant and one Countywide rate.
Commissioner Adkinson stated so legally they cannot.
Attorney Richardson advised right now, legally, because of the structure of the debt and the bond obligations, the debt service has to be generated out of the District.
Commissioner Adkinson stated her next point is, and she asked because she is hearing Barefoot Bay, if Mr. Fontanin could make it better for them rather than what was originally continuing to rise over the next years; and he checked, did some recalculations, and he is telling her it can be rolled back and frozen for a while.
Mr. Fontanin stated assuming the Board goes down the path to approve sunsetting Barefoot Bay, then calculate the user rate for Barefoot Bay, the calculation changes because it is no longer an entity for perpetuity, it would be an entity for four years; staff has done that where it can roll it back to the 2025 rates and flat line it from that point on until the sunset period; she knows the Commissioner asked him the question and the Assistant County Manager, Jill Hayes, fact checked it for him, and the answer is there is $4.5 million left in the bond.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she does not know the answer to this; and she asked if the costs are estimated, if someone is reading the meter monthly, or how does that work in Barefoot Bay.
Mr. Fontanin replied one of the things that have been done in Barefoot Bay, the County has taken over the really old utility, so they have invested in replacing all the residential water meters; he stated it is all by radio reading; one person can do more than 5,000 readings because all it consists of is driving down the road at 25 to 30 miles per hour and it records it; there is ample personnel in order to do that; and if any of the residents have a discrepancy in the bill, please let the Department know.
Commissioner Adkinson stated if anybody has a serious concern about bills being wildly wrong, if they brought them to her they can clearly bring them to staff; but if they brought them to her, she could also bring them to Mr. Fontanin.
Mr. Fontanin replied affirmatively.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if he would look at them specifically.
Mr. Fontanin responded affirmatively stating and because of the radio read, it provides a diurnal of what the water flow is; he is a homeowner, he had a high water bill, he had the water department pull it from the water meter, and the guy asked him literally if he was throwing parties at 2:00 a.m. because he had a slow leak; and staff has that data now to check that.
Ms. Pearl stated she would someone to clarify if the people can read their own meters; she does nothing they are being read; the maintenance department hangs out under the trees all day and they still get paid; she does not see how elderly couples have bills of $200 to $300; like she said early her routines never changed in the six years that she has been there; and it started at $50, now it is $100; and she would like to know if the people can read their own meters.
Mr. Fontanin stated it is not like an old school meter where it has a dial on it and people could actually read the numbers, it is all electronic; if any resident wants to see the data of that, the Department can provide it; for the circumstances, staff gets a variety of issues or dynamics associated with bills so it would be tough to say this is reason for any high bills.
Ms. Pearl asked how people would go about requesting that data monthly.
Mr. Fontanin advised to contact the billing office.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if one would just need to contact the billing office to request that.
Mr. Fontanin responded affirmatively.
Ms. James asked if she may give Commissioner Adkinson a tiny bit of that argument of why the other Commissioners might want to go along with this plan; she mentioned both groups would have more residential customers to share the cost associated with repair and maintenance throughout the County; it is truly a win-win; she knows the Board is creative and imaginative; she believes the Board members have a strong moral compass to do the right thing; she thinks the Board can figure out how to pay this debt off and create a new one; and it is barely anything more to the residential customers throughout unincorporated Brevard County, but for the Barefoot Bay residents it would have a profound impact.
Commissioner Feltner stated he also had a small leak and was able to turn everything off to the house and see the digital meter that there was still flow; he was able to find it and have someone come out and fix it; it was not terrible for them; and he asked if the residents can do that with their meters. He inquired if the meters are digital to see that in real time.
Mr. Fontanin noted the radio read meters provide an actual diurnal and he cannot remember but he thinks it holds two or three weeks so they can actually look and see what the water usage is on a 24-hour period over that duration to see.
Commissioner Adkinson commented so they know they have turned everything off, like what Commissioner Feltner is saying, if they know on specific days or whatever that they have turned everything off; and she asked if someone asked for a particular day, staff can see if there is still usage.
Mr. Fontanin responded in the affirmative.
Kevin Heal stated his question is how is it all being managed; all the sites that he has seen all over Brevard County, Florida, and all over the country, he does not think anyone really knows where they have been strategically placed them; water pipes are breaking everywhere; he sees leaks everywhere he goes; the infrastructure is really bad and the County has to protect the people; someone could be tampering with that stuff, water is water; he does not want to go crazy but Iran and all that stuff is going on, and the County has to be careful and protect the people at all cost; and he wants the Board to think about that, how important the infrastructure is. He commented maybe something can be done where the whole State works together to fix this issue.
Chair Altman stated this is a very difficult issue; he remembers when he first came on the Commission in '84, the Commission had just completed implementation of the Clean Water Act; if one multiplies this problem by probably 100 or maybe 1,000, that was the magnitude of the issue they had to deal with; there was dozens of rickety, rackety old sewer treatment, water treatment plants that developers had put in, in the '60s when the wild, wild west was trying to build for the Apollo program; and they had to clean them all up. He noted they had massive rate increases; he does not know if they had averaged those rates; when they built Sykes Creek and the South Beaches plan, he does not know if they were able to combine the rates to share the impact of the overall cleanup; the question, can they average in with the rest of the County, he thought of that historic time; there was a massive rate increase but they did fix the problem; hats off to the County Commission back in the '70s and '80s, it made it a lot easier for its predecessors; and he just wonders if there is any precedent there in the way they handled that, that could be applied today.
Attorney Richardson stated he is reading the minutes from the meeting and it is the exact same discussion about the equity of the rates, where the base rate in Barefoot Bay is higher; their water use on average is lower, but because the base rate is higher, they still at the time had a higher overall bill than customers outside of the system; the issue was all about what the County inherited with that system that they took over and, bailed out was the term that kept being used back then, and the debt associated with that; there are bond obligations that the County has to comply with, that is why everything is staked to the retirement of the debt; and that is when things can be leveled out and they can come in and be part of the Countywide system.
Chair Altman stated eventually they can get there but not initially.
Attorney Richardson stated this ordinance is the first step to that because it puts a sunset on it establishes a hard date at which the District will be dissolved, when the debt is satisfied.
Chair Altman commented they may achieve it ultimately.
Attorney Richardson noted this is an affirmative statement by the Board that they will get there and when.
Mr. Heal stated the Board mentioned the slow leaking data, and he asked about the large leaking date; he has seen in different areas and all over the State, not just Florida, where there is water running slow leaks and fast leaks and no checking on it for days, months; and he asked who is paying for that.
Commissioner Adkinson stated if there is no further discussion she would like to make the motion to approve legislative intent set forth below and direct staff to prepare an ordinance implementing the intent and schedule and advertise the ordinance for public hearing.
The Board approved legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance to sunset the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District on December 31, 2029; and directed staff to draft the ordinance.
body: Brevard County Board of County Commissioners
matter_type: New Business - Development and Environmental Services Group
title: Legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance sunsetting the Barefoot Bay Water and Sewer District on December 31, 2029, while honoring the existing contractual obligations and commitments of the District.

Juanita Jackson, Housing and Human Services Director, stated this Item is the creation of the Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee and amending to the Together in Partnership (TIP) Citizen Advisory Committee to remove opioid funding and responsibilities; on December 7, 2021, the Board approved an amendment to the TIP Resolution to establish two subcommittees, including representation from the municipalities; under the TIP Advisory Board, the two subcommittees were charged with making suggestions on which approved uses to address and fund with opioid settlement funding, oversee the Request for Application (RFA) process, and make funding recommendations to the Board; after several years of administering opioid settlement funds, Housing and Human Services proposes removing the opioid review and recommendations committee from the TIP Advisory Board structure and establish a standalone advisory committee to be known as, the Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee; this will be in line with the our Advisory Committees; and the Opioid Misuse Advisory Committee shall serve as an advisory committee to the Board and to County Administration regarding planning, implementation, and oversight of opioid settlement funding activities. She continued by saying the structure will be as such to make sure Brevard County remains a qualified County; a representative from the City of Melbourne, City of Palm Bay, a representative from Space Coast League of Cities, a representative from Brevard County Government, a representative from Brevard County Sheriff’s Department, and the four remaining at-large seats will be chosen as citizens from the community involvement; and with the approval of the creation of Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee as a separate standalone advisory committee, it is further requested that the existing Opioid Review and Recommendation Subcommittees be removed from TIP, including the standing committee seats that were added for the qualified County purposes.
The Board adopted Resolution No. 26-054, establishing the creation of Opioid Misuse Abatement Advisory Committee, and Resolution No. 26-055, amending the TIP Citizen Advisory Committee, upon approval by the County Attorney and Risk Management.

Chair Altman read into the record Item J.5. is legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance creating the Brevard Barrier Island Area of Critical State Concern Land Authority.
Larissa Ozols stated she is in attendance tonight to ask for a formal deferral of this Item; the summary item states that the funds will be acquired from the Sebastian Inlet Park; for the next six or seven years that is going to be under construction specifically with the laydown and temporary parking being half of what it is right now; the question in front of everyone is how is it going to get funded; she inquired if there is legislative intent this evening, should people not have the idea of how it is going to get funded for real, has this been considered; she mentioned there is nothing in the summary statement; it was advertised on the 26th, and today is the 7th, so she does not know if this is really the time; and she is formally requesting the Board to defer the Item until a later date.
Mark Shantzis stated the end product is ditto to that; he is the Executive Director of the Barrier Island Preservation Protection Association (BIPPA); it was formed in 1990, over 35 years ago, to help balance the population growth on the beaches with the natural habitat and wildlife; a great deal of it is the sea turtles, which is the largest area of Loggerhead sea turtle hatchlings in the world; he is concerned, but trying to be positive about this; he is an entrepreneur and spent his whole life doing new things, but he just has not had time to really review as he just found out about it four or five days ago, accidentally; the area of critical state concern was put together by BIPPA, which is his organization; the community, Sea Turtle Conservancy, Thousand Friends of Florida, legislators, and a bunch of other people have not reviewed this at all and he thinks they should have the opportunity to review this before it goes to advertisement or before any tax dollars are spent on it or for the County to use their employees, which are the people’s employees, the people’s tax dollars, to start developing an ordinance; the Ordinance in Monroe County is interesting, it was formed in 1986; he asked if anybody has gone to the Keys lately, and does anyone notice it is an area of critical state concern; he commented the development there and the vacation rentals there are a mess; and down to the issue of who are going to be the people of the five volunteer advisers on this, he asked who is going to oversee them. He went on to say then there is the issue of bonding; this land authority is a specialized authority and it is going to have the ability to do bonding, bonding to an extremely small area of people and there are 5,000 people that are going to pay off some bond that this Commission may not approve it, but a future Commission may approve something that is outrageous, then the people will end up with some general obligation bond, possibly; no one knows what the ramification are; what the people do want, is to know that the State supports it, but the State has not been notified, in his opinion, or that he knows of; he has spoken with people there and they say they do not know anything about it; he does not think the Sea Turtle Conservancy has supported it, the community has not been contacted, and he noticed there is no core mission for this; he thinks there should be a core mission rather than wide open to whatever the land authority is; and in the end there needs to be talk about the funding mechanism. He noted the Inlet is not going to be able to fund anything; there is a very poor funding mechanism; there is not much tourism going on down there, only three or four little motels; and hitting them with additional taxes is just not appropriate. He went on to say he thinks the Board should defer this to a later date, get everybody in a workshop, sitting down at the table; the people who developed the area of critical state concern can get together and develop the land authority with proper input from everybody who started it in the first place; and he asked to give them time to all get together and do that. He noted he is trying to be positive, he thinks it is a good idea; and he does not know what the negatives are or what the tentacles look like.
Sandra Sullivan stated the Board was just talking about Barefoot Bay with 5,000 people paying off a bond and that is about the same population size for the South Beaches; with a special district just do an analogy, in order for a special district to do a bond, it has to be by referendum; the Board cannot take a vote and create a special district and then do a bond, that is not the way it works; if anybody remembers, Scott Ellis, former Clerk of the Court, sued the County over the bond that was created for Blue Origin; and when it comes to creating an entity that has the ability to issue bonds, she thinks if the Board is going to do a land authority, this should go out to referendum to District 3 for the residents in that area to vote on it because this is talking about potentially creating debt. She continued by saying she was at the meeting for the area of critical state concern; there were hundreds of people there, a lot of community engagement was part of that process and respecting the people down there; they are very passionate about the area of critical state concern; it is a wonderful thing and thanks to Commissioner Altman that spearheaded this and got this across the line; it will be one of those things 20 or 30 years from now that people will know as one of the remarkable things like the Archie Carr Preserves; it is just very impactful; she would just say that there needs to be communication about what the intent is to the people down there; and if the Board does decide to do a land authority, she thinks the Board should strongly consider that it goes to referendum because it is talking about debt.
Commissioner Adkinson advised she has been in contact with a lot of the South Beach residents, which is sort of how this came to be; the idea originally of the area of critical state concern was to protect and preserve that area; recently, the State has taken some steps that makes that a little more vulnerable; her intention with this is to have an advisory board by the people who live there; it would be five people who live in that area who will be advising this Board on the steps they can take to safeguard their community; people who live outside will not be on the advisory board; it is really important to her that the people who live there are the ones making all of the suggestions to this Board of five people who may not live there; and the idea is to make sure that they have as much control as possible of their area because the way she feels is that the State is slowly taking that away. She went on to say how to decide to pick those five people is yet to be determined; right now she is asking for legislative intent; while it might be new to some of the residents, this has been ongoing for quite a while; she has been talking to lots of residents because she lives a quarter-mile from the beginning and grew up down there, so she has lots of ties and contacts to the people who still live there; she is asking for legislative intent; and the idea of how to fund it, Sebastian State Park may not be the only way to fund it, but to put it off does not make sense, even though there is going to be construction. She asked why put off even funding it a little bit if it can be done now.
Commissioner Feltner stated he did not know that Sebastian Park is going to be under construction for a while.
Commissioner Adkinson responded yes, the bridge.
Commissioner Feltner stated oh the bridge.
Commissioner Adkinson remarked it is interesting because they would only be able to collect revenue…
Commissioner Feltner interjected by saying on the north side.
Commissioner Adkinson finished by saying, exactly; she explained even after the bridge is complete because even though the area of critical state concern extends past that into Indian River County, she thinks staff was asked to check into its counterpart down in Indian River; and these are all the things that legislative intent will allow the Board to look at and figure out going forward.
Commissioner Feltner stated this is what he split with Commissioner Adkinson today; creating the advisory board would be one thing; maybe with their help she could come up with some funding mechanism later that takes into consideration…
Commissioner Adkinson interrupted by saying she thinks the statute says that they have 90 days to create a funding mechanism; she asked if the County Attorney, Morris Richardson, knows; and she mentioned she believes somewhere in her notes it says that.
Attorney Richardson stated if the Board creates a land authority, the State has to be begin remitting that surcharge of the State Park within 90 days.
Commissioner Adkinson asked Commissioner Feltner what he is suggesting.
Commissioner Feltner replied hold on, he is getting there; if is it not a land authority, it is an advisory board maybe in the first stage; then say they create their charter; start thinking like that; there is the advisory board and their first mission is to work on a Charter and that contains several things, the funding mechanism, potentially scope and some of that other stuff; and then call it a land authority, upgrade it after there is a charter.
Attorney Richardson stated before this gets too far down the road, the Board is the land authority by statute, it just puts on a different hat.
Commissioner Feltner stated okay.
Attorney Richardson continued by saying there is an advisory board that advises the land authority.
Commissioner Feltner stated receiving written notice regarding the creation of a land authority.
Attorney Richardson commented the Board creates the land authority, but the Board of County Commissioners is the governing Board of the land authority, then there is an advisory board to the land authority; but the advisory board is not the land authority.
Commissioner Feltner explained he was looking for a step in the process; there could be appointed people…
Commissioner Adkinson interjected by saying she thinks once the Board creates the land authority, then it can decide how to create the advisory board; and then that advisory board can do exactly what Commissioner Feltner is saying, advise the Board how they want to proceed, their goals, their mission statement.
Commissioner Feltner commented the issue is it has to be decided from the beginning how it is going to be funded; and he asked if that is correct.
Commissioner Adkinson replied the Board does not have to fund them, but she thinks it would be the smart thing to do if it is going to create it, then it should fund it.
Commissioner Feltner mentioned that is what he is trying to figure out because he thinks there are some legitimate questions with that, and if it could come back later on the funding part of it.
Commissioner Adkinson stated she could come back later if that would make him more comfortable about funding.
Chair Altman stated he thinks if it is not funded it guts the intent; he thinks this is a really good thing for the South Beaches; having been very much involved in the South Beaches for much of his life, he likes the idea and can understand why everyone wants to be a part of it and have input; that opportunity will arise, the Board has to advertise an ordinance and get input; what this does is it creates an entity, a land authority, that has the mission to preserving the South Beaches; it has the ability to make recommendations for land use changes, land acquisition, and does all the things that those who supported the area of critical state concern wanted to see; and he is kind of excited about it.
Commissioner Adkinson stated as advised by people who live there.
Chair Altman replied right, it gives local control; he commented the other thing is the fees are modest; it is visitors to the Sebastian Inlet State Park; unfortunately, most of those visitors are on the south side, but the influx of people coming to the park are from all over the State; at one point she thinks it was the single largest visited State park in the entire system; and they do have impact on the South Beaches, so it is a fair use that they participate. He noted he does not have any problems with it; he would support moving ahead with an ordinance which requires advertising; it gives ample opportunity for the residents down there to give feedback; and he thinks it is a wonderful proposal.
Mr. Shantzis stated the area of critical state concern was created by the community because of a Commissioner that was going to pave everything over and all the other Commissioners sat there and did not say anything, they sat there and watched it happen; the residents did not want to be bothered to have to go to the State; they did not want to have to go and have the State override the Commission; they had, what they thought was an unthinkably bad Commission; this Board is not that, it is a great Commission as far as he is concerned, but there are no guarantees in the future that that will be the case; there could be somebody who comes in and… the people are not helping the decision by advising; the Board is the decision maker, and this Board will not be there in the future, guaranteed, it will be other people there; no matter who advises them, the Board members will vote the way they want; the reason that the residents went to the State in the first place; they do not want to have to do that again; but it will happen again. He went on to say this is the most developable area in the entire United States, everybody wants it; there will be a Commission in the future that will bail; it is not this Board; the residents do not want to be in that situation; he does not think it is a bad idea, but they want to put in the caveats in the beginning before they start advertising and spend tax dollars creating an ordinance where everyone is just going to go on their merry way and there will not be a workshop, and they will not end up with anything; he mentioned that Commissioner Feltner can set up an advisory committee of these five people and these different organizations first; have the workshop, have them create the guts of what this is going to be to protect the residents since they are the ones, the Sea Turtle Conservancy, the community, Thousand Friends, BIPPA, and even Commissioner Altman, who created this around the Commission; that was the idea; and he asked the Board to not put them in that situation again. He asked the Board to postpone this; he mentioned with El Niño, there is a really good chance that there will not be a landfall this year; if there is no landfall by hurricane season 2027, 180 is gone; he commented why jump ahead and create this when it is conceivable that it will not be necessary; and then the talk about bonding for a small amount of people if there is a bad Commission, 5,000 people, who knows what it will want to do there.
Chair Altman stated he thinks if Mr. Shantzis were to ask Thousand Friends of Florida, he has a strong inclination that they would support this.
Mr. Shantzis replied so ask them; if the Board asked Thousand Friends of Florida, the Sea Turtle Conservancy, BIPPA, and the community, but Commissioner Adkinson has not talked to 5,000 people, guaranteed, nor has she talked to one percent of 5,000 people; he is talking about 1,000 people showing up at the Commission in order to talk about vacation rentals; he is talking about BIPPA activates the community, and BIPPA was not contacted; he thinks that was a bad move; and it does not mean it cannot be corrected, he thinks it can be corrected.
Chair Altman stated he is going to stop this; he allowed Mr. Shantzis to come up and speak…
Mr. Shantzis noted he is trying to be as positive as her can, but to move forward with this thing…
Chair Altman interjected by saying he does not want to create a point counterpoint type situation.
Mr. Shantzis remarked he is just telling the Board there is more risk to this thing if it moves forward now without postponing it; and it can be done in the future.
Chair Altman commented he thinks it is a great thing.
Ms. Ozols stated she will be brief but she wanted to read into the record the powers of the land authority; the first one is to sue or be sued; this is from Florida Statute, within 380.0553 Brevard Barrier Island Protection Designation area of critical concern; the powers of the land authority are broad and they are vast, and are permanent and they are written in the Florida State Statute; to be sued or sue, to undertake, carry out studies, obviously, to acquire dispose of real property, personal property of any interest therein, such acquisition is necessary or appropriate to protect the natural environment, which is great, provide public access, that is great too, but there is also the area of bonding that is also written into this statute, which allows all the future Boards then to bond this small little population; and she thanked Board and asked for it to be deferred this evening.
Chair Altman stated he wants to say to Mr. Shantzis, Ms. Ozola, and Commissioner Adkinson, he loves them both and he thinks the world of them, but he does not want to see them get into an argument; he finds it incredibly ironic that everyone has the same goal and this hurts the South beaches; they all want to get there they just have a difference of opinion…
Attorney Richardson stated he does not know if it helpful to the conversation or not but the bonding that people seem fixated on, it can only secure payment of the bond debt with the revenues that are generated through the statutory mechanisms, which are the surcharge at the State park and the incremental tourist tax that would be imposed on a few facilities down there; the ability to bond would be virtually nothing; it could never be a general revenue bond obligation that is payable by the taxpayers of the South Beaches, or something like that; to the extent that has been voiced as a concern, it is not a thing; and likely there would never be a bond issue because those revenue sources are so limited that they would not be sufficient to service bond debt.
Chair Altman stated one of the things he likes about the authority is the ability to seek out grants, ability to qualify for State funding and special projects, federal funding, environmental programs, and partnering with other environmental entities is a positive.
Commissioner Adkinson pointed out this also gives the residents of the South Beaches a direct voice to the Commissioners; as an advisory board they are being requested and the Commissioners want to hear what they have to say and they have to hear what they have to say; and right now, the Commissioners do not have to listen to anybody in the South Beaches if he or she does not want to.
Commissioner Feltner stated he thinks he agrees there is a very small limited ability to collect revenue to service debt in the way of a bond; he thinks Tax Increment Financing (TIF) funding is going to be next to nothing; He apologized stating he meant Tourist Development Tax (TDT); he asked that the financial part be taken out, there will not be bonds because it is going to be next to nothing; then she will have the rest of it; and he asked if Commissioner Adkinson would do that tonight.
Commissioner Adkinson commented she does not think putting something together and not funding it is appropriate so she is ready to make a motion; and she moved to approve legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance creating the Barrier Island Area Land Authority and direct staff to draft the ordinance.
Commissioner Feltner advised he will second, but he thinks Commissioner Adkinson will probably get very little revenue, so just to clarify, the Board has to approve any sort of bond; and he asked if that is correct.
Attorney Richardson advised the Board is the land authority so it would be the one seeking the bonding and it would be limited to the…
Commissioner Feltner interjected saying the revenue which would be next to nothing.
Attorney Richardson agreed.
The Board approved legislative intent and permission to advertise an ordinance creating the Brevard Barrier Island Area Land Authority; and directed staff to draft the ordinance.
body: Brevard County Board of County Commissioners
title: Legislative Intent and Permission to Advertise an Ordinance creating the Brevard Barrier Island Area of Critical State Concern Land Authority

action_text:
Chair Altman apologized for leaving out the three cards from the first public comment section of the agenda and noted those will be heard first if they are still in attendance.
Mark Shropshire stated one of the things on the Agenda is the intersection at Canaveral Groves Boulevard and Grissom; he would like to start with an antidote; he knows it is not a good way to make an argument but many years ago at Thanksgiving time coming home late at night, his family came across a car turned over, smoking, dust everywhere, and it was a nightmare situation; he sat for about an hour with two small children while their mother died on the other side of the car; they still had to be airlifted out; it is appalling to him after living there for so long, how many deaths happen at that stretch of road; he has been thinking about it for many years; and he thinks it has to do with people coming through that intersection extremely fast. He noted his story would be anecdotal if it was not for other deaths, numerous deaths that happen at the intersection and along the road; all his family members have come across something horrible at one time or another; his appeal is for the Board to consider a traffic circle; he know everybody hates a traffic circle, but nobody dies at traffic circles; and that is his main point, so please consider it. He continued by saying he does not think it is a big expense to change.
Chair Altman stated he just wants to thank Mr. Shropshire for sitting through the meeting and bringing such an important issue.
Mr. Shropshire responded by saying he felt like it was worth it.
Chair Altman stated he will direct staff, but unfortunately there is not a Commissioner at his disposal for District 1.
Mr. Shropshire stated he mentioned it to Commissioner Delaney.
Chair Altman stated all the Commissioners have committed to pulling together to help support District 1 during this period; he asked staff to get together and look at potential options and also reach out to the Sheriff’s Department to see what is happening as far as enforcement; he is talking about traffic calming which is a wonderful way of gaining control; he knows that very well, his wife used to teach at Challenger 7; it is a wonderful place with a lot of young families; and the Board will see what it can do. He added his staff will follow up with Mr. Shropshire soon.
Rick Heffelfinger inquired if the Board is still going to get the impact fee study.
Chair Altman stated he will ask staff as he is not a big fan of impact fees.
Mr. Heffelfinger mentioned he knows Chair Altman is not a fan, but the County already did a big impact fee with the water.
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, stated yes.
Mr. Heffelfinger asked if the public will get that at the next meeting; Marc Bernath gave a presentation to the Citizen Budget Review and said they were still working on it because the staff had to give them input in order to do the study; now he realizes that is probably going to come by events, but there was transportation impact and all that stuff; they will be hit hard on water as the Board already voted for that; and he would hope the Board would consider that as getting the new people instead of the old people. He continued by saying one of the topics being talked about was how to get money for Municipal Service Taxing Unit (MSTUs) from these big developments; the Board might want to look at what they did at Windward Preserve, down at the end of his street; of course it required a lawsuit, but part of that lawsuit made the developer have to pay for road improvements because they are County roads; this Board did a right-of-way transfer to the City of Cocoa and the City of Cocoa said that the Community Development District (CDD), or something like a homeowners association, have responsibility for the feeder road although it is a public road; therefore there are ways around making a community like that pay for stuff; he does not know that it takes a lawsuit; and again, that was a played game with the County and City. He added it was a mess but they put speed humps down a County road and paid for it; Commissioner Pritchett made sure they put guardrails too; he hopes that was not paid for by the County; and someone said it was not going to be as it was part of the settlement, but they also paved that. He stated they built that road for their development; if they put sidewalks on it, they will pay for those too because they are required for maintenance; there is one way to do it, one just has to stipulate when the development comes in that they are going to make road improvements; theoretically, they could have paid for a wonderful roundabout, which was looked at, at one point; the Board can do anything it wants if it says a feeder road, make improvements, or pay MSTU, as they are in Cocoa and have to pay the County MSTU as part of the Agreement as well; and the County used that lawsuit opportunity, they did not file it, some private party did. He noted the County got involved and said they were going to give the County MSTU as part of the settlement; they did not start collecting them until just now, when people move it; but the mechanism was there and it was still part of that lawsuit so that is probably something; what he really wanted to do was ask a question; he became aware of a letter that was written by Thea Thorne and she had some wonderful suggestions for the County about water, District 1 in particular; he thinks it went to the County Manager and he forwarded it onto the staff for District 1, it may have gone to Marc Bernath, he does not know; he would love to find out how the public is going to get some feedback from that; and he wants everybody to be aware of this wonderful letter.
William Porter stated he is there because of a situation that he has; he will get straight to the point; this is in May 4, of 2021, where he has approval of two RVs that are on the side of his home; they have been there for 15 years, as long as he has; in 2023, some neighbors that had purchased property had filed with the County to have the RVs removed; he is pretty sure they filed the first case where they were approved to be there; it had been an ongoing thing and they had already been approved in 2009; and in 2023 it was found in the transcripts that he no longer has enough room due to the setbacks for the side yard. He noted there are no setbacks for side yard so they used a different code, 1340, and he will not go into the depths of it; regardless, he went through quite a spell; the RV has to meet a setback and it is not; it says parking locating RV and meeting the proper setback of seven and one-half feet from either side of the line; line for RV is a stored side yard next to a black chain fence so it does not have room in the setback at all, so the trailers would have to be removed, the two RVs; later because of the 2021 and the 2009 approvals, he already knew that was incorrect; he went through quite a bit of money and quite a bit of troubles; then this date is February 6, 2024, it was found that the RVs were in fact in Code; where he is at now, is they are still there as they have been, in Code the whole time, but now he is sitting with a $900 fine, where he has already paid $695 in fines and fees, and some he does not have a clue about what; and he has another to pay the costs of the RV sitting there of $3,647, so it comes up to where now he owes the County for the RV sitting where they are now for the time frame it took to find that they were in compliance of Code after all and he is being fined and owes $4,500 to the County because he still has the RVs and they are in Code. He commented he is not sure if he needs to be here to discuss this because he does not understand where these actual costs come from, they never come by to look at anything.
Chair Altman stated he thinks that is a legal issue; it probably will not be resolved here tonight, but staff should look into that; he is looking at a picture of his property right now and he sees the RVs; and they are in Code.
Mr. Porter stated they have been there for 20 years now.
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, stated staff will get his contact information and have someone call him to see what is going on.
Mr. Porter stated he would appreciate that, he does not have $4,500 anymore.
Chair Altman commented he will ask the County Attorney, if Mr. Porter prevailed and was found within Code…
Mr. Liesenfelt stated staff will look at everything too.
Morris Richardson, County Attorney, commented he can get in contact with the Code Enforcement people and get it figured out.
Chair Altman noted he will follow up.
Attorney Richardson pointed him in the direction of the Planning and Development Director, Billy Prasad.

action_text:
Commissioner Feltner stated he has a question for Edward Fontanin, Utility Services Director; the Board heard about Space Florida earlier; and he asked for Mr. Fontanin to give an update on what he knows regarding their needs for wastewater.
Mr. Fontanin explained as the Board knows staff is working with Jacobs engineering on the phase two of the Port; there have been a lot of shareholder meetings; part of that includes the U.S. Air Forces, the Space Force, National Aeronautical Space Administration (NASA), and Space Florida; recently, in the past three or four weeks, the U.S. Air Force and himself, and he differentiates between the Air Force and Space Force because it is a Space Force Station, but the wastewater plant on the facility is an Air Force asset; with that being said the Air Force has made an announcement that they are going to build a new wastewater plant adjacent to their existing plant with the intention of providing capacity needed for the future, associated with NASA; and it also seems like Space Florida would have capacity there. He went on to say this has been done at the meetings with the Economic Development Commission (EDC); they have received confirmation from the two colonels, one representing the Air Force, and one representing Space Force; staff has asked Space Florida to provide them what their new direction is because now that this dynamic has changed their direction on whether they want to connect into the Sykes Creek plant; in the meantime, what County has fallen through on the commitment to draft an agreement for Space Florida; a solid draft is ready to go, the only thing they are waiting for Space Florida is to confirm they are still on the direction, which the Board was in February 2024, where this was the discussion and the Board direction about the $130 million investment; if Space Florida is intending to connect into the Air Force wastewater plant, there is no need for the magnitude of pipe needed for Space Force to come down to the County’s wastewater plant, even if they wanted some sort of redundant, it would be much smaller; and he does not think it would be the $130 million impact to the wastewater plant based on those flows. He continued by saying staff has reached out to Space Florida to seek confirmation on what direction they are going; once they get that direction they can come back to the Board to get authorization from the Board to proceed on that new direction; and from there staff can proceed.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing to consider Sunshine State Wildlife Conservation LLC and Bernard Eagan & Company requesting a CUP for land alteration in AU and GU (25Z00061) (Tax Account Nos. 3001213, 3001181, 3020488, 3020489, and part of 3001207, 3030338, and 3030339).
Tim Craven, Senior Planner, Planning and Development, stated Item H.3. is Sunshine State Wildlife Conservation LLC and Bernard Egan and Company, Ralph Brown is representing, requesting a CUP for land alteration in AU and GU, zoning application 25Z00061, and it is located in District 5.
Ralph Brown stated he works for Blue Goose Survey and Design and they are the applicant for the Sunshine State Mine; he wanted to clarify that this is the third phase of the mine that they are in for, so they have already permitted about 540 acres of the mine with the County and with the Water Management District; the mine has been in operation for about six years; when looking at the CUP application number, the Board will see that the project is 723 acres, that is a combination of all three phases together; and the only new thing they are in for is phase three which is more like 187 acres. He continued by saying the mine has been in operation for six years; it is located off of Babcock Street, just north of the C-54 Canal; all access is off of Babcock through the driveway that was permitted back in phase one; there are no new connections to roads; and they are utilizing the existing infrastructure that was permitted six years ago. He noted the density, they are proposing three new mining cells which total about 78 acres, but the project acreage is 186 acres; they are really using about 40 percent of the property for actual construction of mining cells, and the rest is preserved with trees or wetlands; he just thought there was an impression that this was a new mine that maybe was 723 acres; and he just wanted to clarify that really it is the third phase of a mine that has been going on for six years.
Chair Altman stated Mr. Brown had mentioned that 40 percent of the property will be excavated.
Mr. Brown advised in the third phase, yes.
Chair Altman asked if the rest of the property will have preserved trees and preservation of wetlands; and does that mean Mr. Brown has no intention of developing the rest of the property, or would it be in preserve.
Mr. Brown responded it may be developed in the future, but they have no wetland impacts, and they have quite a few trees on the property; all of the stockpile of materials can be back in the previous phases that are already constructed; but he will not commit to there not being any future development.
Chair Altman asked if he was not making any representations of what density that may be; and does he have potable water at this site.
Mr. Brown replied no.
Chair Altman noted and no sewer; and he noticed that this is very close proximity to the Sebastian State Preserve and Goodwin’s.
Mr. Brown remarked it is across on the other side of Babcock; and on the east side of Babcock is the buffer preserve property.
Chair Altman asked has there been any comments from St. John’s River Water Management District (SJRWMD) or Florida Department of Environment Protection (FDEP); and he asked staff if they have reviewed the impacts of the mining expansion to the north.
Mr. Brown stated just to clarify, they do have their permits already from SJRWMD, they have already issued the permits for phase three, phase two, and phase one.
Jane Hart, Environmental Specialist, Natural Resources Management, replied if the question is have they received their St. John’s permit, the answer is yes.
Chair Altman asked if there were any reviews or comments on behalf . . . he means they have permits, so he guesses one of the questions he has, he knows Goodwin’s Preserve, as well, is a very critical and strategic water fowl area; in the excavation, depth, and he sees he has side wall profiles of the . . . He asked if there has been any consideration to support those or have a water fowl, or is it strictly a very deep hole, 40 foot depth, which would be very limited in terms of water fowl; but any of the littoral zones, has there been any effort to support some of the needs down there.
Mr. Brown pointed out they do have five to one on the mine reclamation plan, so the County will end up with vegetated slopes, some wetland vegetation on the slopes.
Chair Altman asked if he will be planting wetland vegetation in those slopes.
Mr. Brown responded that is not required at this time, they have not proposed that; but they are preserving about 10 wetland areas which would provide habitat.
Chair Altman asked if the five to one slopes are to the waterline, or below the waterline.
Mr. Brown replied below the waterline.
Chair Altman asked how far from the waterline does that go, how far does it reach into the lake.
Mr. Brown advised it goes five foot below the waterline, so there is a normal water level and a five to one slope goes five feet vertically down from that waterline.
Chair Altman stated so it is five to one from the waterline, so . . .
Mr. Brown interjected by saying five to one from the top, all the way down five foot below what they expect to be the water level in the lake.
Chair Altman inquired how far from the shore is that five to one slope.
Mr. Brown stated so that would be at a five to one slope that is going out almost 50 foot.
Chair Altman asked 50 feet from the shoreline.
Mr. Brown replied yes.
Chair Altman stated he noticed that the water depth of these pits, lakes is going to be 40 feet.
Mr. Brown advised yes.
Chair Altman pointed out that is incredibly deep for Florida; but he assumes that was approved by the SJRWMD; and he asked has the County environmental . . . are there other lakes that deep.
Mr. Brown mentioned it is a standard depth; the purpose of their mine is to mine general fill that is used for house pads and then also to mine rock, which goes down to 40 feet; the rock is used for road base, roads, aggregates, like 57 stone and all that; there are two mines to the north of them that are also 40 feet or deeper; and the mines that get beach sand actually go down to 80, 90, 100 foot deep, so 40 is a standard depth for mines.
Chair Altman asked at that depth, is it their intention to use these for stormwater retention.
Mr. Brown responded they could be used for stormwater retention in the future.
Chair Altman stated he knows there has been discussion about when there is a lake that deep and one uses surface water to flow into those lakes, there is a potential of contaminating the aquifer below, he was just curious; but of course, he would have to get St. John’s, and he assumes County permitting for that.
Mr. Craven stated if the County did it in the future it would.
Ms. Hart advised yes, it would have to go through County review.
Chair Altman stated and the Water Management District he thinks.
Ms. Hart remarked yes.
Mr. Brown pointed out the Water Management District recently changed their rules, so a wet stormwater pond by itself cannot be used to meet their criteria; if this was going to be permitted in the future, one would have to have basically a treatment pond that then discharged into the wet pond; the wet pond could be used for flood storage; but it probably would not be used for the water quality of it.
Chair Altman stated okay, that is good. He asked if there are any endangered species on the site.
Mr. Brown replied no, they had a Caracara and a wetland study that was done by a consultant and nothing was found.
Chair Altman commented he is very familiar with the area; it is an amazing area; he is also familiar with North Indian River County, he used to represent that area; he knows the community; he knows 25 percent of their trucks go south; and he asked if Mr. Brown has had any complaints from Indian River County residents . . .
Mr. Brown responded no.
Chair Altman stated for the increased truck in a relatively rural area, Fellsmere.
Mr. Brown noted yes, they go through Fellsmere, a lot more traffic to the north.
Chair Altman stated right.
Mr. Brown stated there is a lot more development in Brevard County than there is in Indian River County.
Chair Altman asked again if he has any problems with complaints; he stated he has spoken with some folks there about that; it is intense; but they have done a good job here in their permit application he reviewed quite in detail.
Mr. Brown expressed his appreciation to Chair Altman.
Chair Altman stated he would love to have an opportunity to go out and look at it physically; he has driven by there numerous times; but he reiterated he would love the opportunity to see it firsthand; and he knows that material is very important.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board approved the request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) for land alteration in AU and GU (25Z000061) (Tax Accounts 3001213, 3001181, 3020488, 3020489, and part of 3001207, 3030338, and 30303389).

action_text:
The Board of County Commissioners acts as a Quasi-Judicial body when it hears request for
rezoning and Conditional Use Permits. Applicants must provide competent substantial evidence
establishing facts, or expert witness opinion testimony showing that the request meets the
Zoning Code and Comprehensive Plan criteria. Opponents must also testify as to facts, or
provide expert testimony; whether they like, or dislike, a request is not competent evidence.
The Board must then decide whether the evidence demonstrates consistency and compatibility
with the Comprehensive Plan and the existing rules in the Zoning Ordinance, property adjacent
to the property rezoned, and the actual development of the surrounding area. The Board
cannot consider speculation, non-expert opinion testimony, or poll the audience by asking
those in favor or opposed to stand up or raise their hands. If a Commissioner has had
communications regarding a rezoning or Conditional Use Permit request before the Board,
Commissioner must disclose the subject of the communication and the identity of the person,
group, or entity, with whom the communication took place before the Board takes action on the
request. Each applicant is allowed a total of 15 minutes to present their request unless the
time is extended by a majority vote of the Board. The applicant may reserve any portion of the
15 minutes for rebuttal. Other speakers are allowed five minutes to speak. Speakers may not
pass their time to someone else in order to give that person more time to speak.

title: CONSENT AGENDA (The entire Consent Agenda will be passed in one motion to include everything under Section F.)

action_text:
Billy Prasad, Planning and Development Director, explained this is a Findings of Fact for the denial of a request for a change of zoning classification from AU with a Binding Site Plan (BSP) to RU-2-15 and RU-2-30, with removal of BSP on property owned by Merritt Bidco SPV, LLC.
Richard Heffelfinger commented he hopes consent means the Commissioners already said it is a go, and no Commissioner pulled it; and he asked if the Board is going to agree to this Findings of Fact. He stated he means that thing on Merritt Island is going to be a denied zoning and it is not going to happen; and he asked if that is true.
Chair Altman stated it is not in the question and answer, but the Board wants to hear his input.
Mr. Heffelfinger stated the one on Merritt Island, the Board did a Findings of Fact, and he thinks Morris Richardson, County Attorney, is the one who did that; he thinks one of the big reasons the Board is going to say no is that the applicant was going to flood SR 3, which is a State Road; but still the Comprehensive Plan, or whatever, says the Board can consider that; the Findings of Fact said that was true; the reason it is a Consent Agenda, and the Findings of Fact founded, is because of these people back here, they did good; he thinks it sets a precedent that when the County has these, if people do not speak up, they could have gotten railroaded; whoever it was, he knows there were a couple of people who were a lead on that; and he wants to go on the record to say the Board needs to do this more if the County wants to try to control its neighborhoods. He expressed his appreciation to everybody; he stated a lot of them are sitting back here; and he reiterated he just wanted to go on record to say that.
Chair Altman expressed his appreciation to staff for presenting a very complete, conclusive set of Findings in the Board’s packet.
The Board adopted Resolution No. 26-056, setting forth the findings of fact and conclusions of the Board pertaining to the denial of a request for a change of zoning classification from AU with a BSP to RU-2-15 and RU-2-30 with removal of BSP on the property owned by Merritt Bidco SPV, LLC.
