action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing on a request by Sami and Violette Salib, represented by Carmine Ferraro, for a Small-Scale Comprehensive Plan Amendment, 26S.05, to change the Future Land Use designation from NC and RES 2 to CC, 26SS00005, tax accounts 2000371 and 2000352, located in District 1.
Trina Gilliam, Planning and Zoning Manager, stated Items H.4., and H.5., are companion applications; she will read them both into the record together, however they will need a separate motion; Sami and Violette Salib, being represented by Carmine Ferraro, requests a Small Scale Comprehensive Plan Amendment under 26S.05 to change the Future Land Use designation from NC and RES 2 to CC, under application 26SS00005, located in District 1; again, Sami and Violette Salib being represented by Carmine Ferraro, requests a change of zoning classification from AU to BU-1, under application 26Z00015, located in District 1; and a little house keeping on this one, there was a discrepancy in the staff report in the Board’s Packet, page 212 and 215 regarding the availability of utility services; there is availability of utility services on this; the writ-up on page 212 is the correct one; also, there is a Binding Development Plan (BDP) that was submitted as well by the applicant; and the BDP states that he will provide a 15-foot vegetative buffer along the northern and eastern boundaries of the subject property. She continued by saying additionally, the developer says he will locate the stormwater retention pond within the northeastern portion of the subject property; it goes on to state in the BDP that the following uses shall be restricted as non-permitted BU-1 zoning, automobile sales and storage, bait and tackle shops, billiards room and electric arcade, group homes both level one and level two, non-overnight commercial parking, gasoline service station, and Planning and Zoning (P&Z) recommended denial and the applicant submitted a non-binding conceptual plan on July 31, after the P&Z meeting which actually depicts a 50 foot natural and planted landscape buffer with a dry retention pond on the northeast portion of the property.
Carmine Ferraro stated he is in attendance on behalf of the property owner, as applicant for the plus or minus seven acres located on the northeast corner of U.S. Highway 1 and Lionel Road; they are seeking a recommendation of approval for a Future Land Use (FLU) change for these two reference tracks; as noted the current FLU for the front track which fronts U.S.1, is Neighborhood Commercial (NC), with the adjoining track which abuts it to the east is residential 2 (RES 2); as part of this action they are also seeking to have both tracks rezoned to be one; he would note as is probably in the Board’s Package, the property to the immediate south has a Dollar General with a Community Commercial (CC) FLU designation and a BU-1 zoning; the intersection tracks north and south of the subject property are a mix of CC and NC; two of the four corners of the intersection are CC, including a 10-unit motel directly across from the property on the west side of U.S.1; and the zoning is also a mixture of BU-1 and BU-2 zoning. He went on to say the zoning category they are seeking is the lesser commercial category of BU-1 which will allow for the targeted uses at this U.S. 1 intersection; the BDP that was mentioned, they offered originally, did not include a gas service gas station, as they received a unanimous recommendation of denial at the Local Planning Agency (LPA) and the P&Z hearing; there was a considerable amount of opposition from local residents and it centered on the intended marketing and use of a gas station; having spoken with the owner, he has since agreed to add as a prohibited use, no gas station, no gas service station; additionally, as was mentioned, they came into the P&Z and the LPA meeting with an offer of a BDP; they have since taken the eastern boundary and increased it to 50 feet and the northern boundary increased to 50 feet as well; when looking at the residences that are on to the north side there will be a 50-foot natural vegetative landscape buffer there and there will additionally be on the north side, the retention pond location which will bring that buffering and distance to roughly 135 feet from the residences; on the east side they notated on the concept plan that it appears that the property is being used as some type of a storage or workshop; but even though there is not a house there, it is zoned residential and they are offering the 50 foot buffer along the entire east side. He continued by saying the intent is that they would be able to have a marketable plat property with these three lots so that his owner can go ahead and sell the property for its highest and best-use value; since they had started this preparation of the second process, they had actually had some other interests in the property unrelated to gas stations; they believe there is a good marketability here on the corner for local commercial and or service businesses; and with that he will leave the rest of his time for rebuttal after the public has spoken unless the Board has any questions for him.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if the natural buffers that will be there, are already there or if they are going to take them down and use something else.
Mr. Ferraro stated the intent is to leave as many of the natural specimen trees in place and remove the noxious vegetation, then plan their landscape buffer for the site plan from that point going back to create an additional buffer.
Billy Gonedridge stated he is the one who owns the property next to that; he spent $165,000 buying that property; he spent another $30,000 just to get power into that and it went in yesterday; he spent another $2,500 for water and that was just for the meter; he spent another $1,500 or $2,000 just to run the water line; he built a metal building out there for about $75,000; he has another $30,000 worth of equipment in it and another $30,000 in a Recreational Vehicle (RV) so he can stay there while his house is being built; he would have never ever bought that property if he knew a gas station or whatever kind of commercial property is going to go in there; he bought it because he knew next door is AU; and he had a buffer. He went on to say he does not want a commercial job or a commercial building next to him, not even with a 50-foot buffer or a 500-foot buffer; he bought it because it was zoned AU and the property next to it was zoned AU; now the Board is changing the rules; this guy wants to change the rules; he does not want the rules changed; he has a lot of money invested in this and he wants to live his dream out there in rural country and live the way he likes to live, private and secure; the commercial-ism he understands, the property in front of it is zoned commercial, and he asked if that is correct; he noted two and one-half acres or 2.3 acres, whatever, that is fine, one can put whatever he or she wants to out there, he does not care, but he does not want it put next to him; and the 50-foot buffer is a joke, he will still see a light shining in his property, either in his bedroom or on the side of his house at midnight, with more people coming out there, and he does not want more people because it brings crime and undesirables. He stated the Dollar General is a problem as it is out there; if one ever drives by out there, just look at the trash on the side of the road; he is adamantly against this; and those are his words.
Commissioner Pritchett asked if Mr. Gonedridge lives off Highway 1 or Lionel Road.
Mr. Gonedridge answered Lionel Road, 3660 right next door; and he can tell the Board right now, if he wants to put a buffer in, that is a joke.
John Hamilton stated his main issue was the gas station; he received a notice that he was 500 feet within the boundaries of that and it scared him; the water system up there is very fragile; several years back there were wells put in north of Mims and Scottsmoor; that actually put bacteria in all of the people’s wells; he had to put in a $5,000 system to clean it; he does not want the gas; and he inquired if the applicant is getting rid of the gas part of it.
Mr. Ferraro replied yes, sir.
Mr. Hamilton commented he is okay with that; he does not mind a business on the front end by U.S.1, but as the gentleman said, he does not want the business right next to his house; he lives just behind him, north on Dunlap Road; it is just a matter of keeping the gas stations out; from there one can go north or south and it is less than five minutes to any gas station, so that is not needed; and he asked if the Board has any questions for him.
Arthur Grunenfelder stated one of his main concerns is he does not know who would come up with putting anything within 500 feet of Pinewood Elementary School where there are kids walking back and forth to school; they are going to get hit, this is dangerous; the people that are going to be at this place, are people who are going to trash the area, they already are trashing the area; by the way, the Dollar General that is there now, that has always been commercial; his brother-in-law, Billy Bellflower, owned it and sold it to them; it has always been commercial and used to be a bar; and basically, putting anything commercial there that far back into that, with the lights and everything, it is a very bad idea. He commented this is stupid; and he asked who the District 1 Commissioner is now.
Commissioner Pritchett advised she is.
Mr. Grunenfelder asked if she is acting until when.
Commissioner Pritchett informed Mr. Grunenfelder until election.
Mr. Grunenfelder inquired if those elections are coming up soon.
Commissioner Pritchett replied yes.
Mr. Grunenfelder stated that is good to know; he just came from 3555 Lionel Road and it took him a little longer to get there because school is out and he has to watch out for the little kids; going down Old Dixie, there are cars parked in the road all the way down coming to pick up their kids from Pinewood; this is going to add to the disaster; like he said he does not know who comes up with this, but it is a very bad idea; and if it means the people need to get signatures or something, just let them know, they would be glad to work with the Board.
Laura Miller stated she lives on Lionel Road and just recently moved there; they moved there from a really congested area in Titusville that was known for a lot of drug activity; when she found the property they bought for $750,000, for 10 acres for her four young boys who are under six years old and go to Pinewood; she was so excited to buy this property, living on cloud nine for the first few months; when she saw the sign that there was going to be a development like this she was shattered; she had envisioned for her boys to be playing outside, they are a very low-tech household; they do not have a television in the house and she had envisioned them playing outside; the thought of that now has kind of been destroyed, thinking about such a high traffic area, especially with her kids going to Pinewood; and she too, is nervous about the traffic, and the people that will be coming so near to a school. She went on to say she has already seen how the development does change a road; since the Dollar General has been built, the traffic has increased; her neighbors brother is a police officer and he sometimes has to call him in to sit there at the end of his road with a radar because the cars are going down the road really fast, she sees it every day; her kids are outside almost all day every day; she got poison ivy all over her face because she was cleaning her beautiful property; she is very disappointed to hear about this potential expansion; her concern is that the Board is not just talking about a one subject thing, they are talking about a rezoning which would allow a lot of different commercial uses; it is a wide range of commercial use; and there is no specific proposal as far as she knows, so the neighbors do not even know what this is, it could be just a broad rezone and then from there could be whatever the owner wanted to build. She noted she would respectfully ask the Board to please consider the long term character of the road and the quiet rural area that Lionel Road has always been; once a commercial zoning has been granted it is very difficult to reverse; and she hopes that Lionel Road can stay the quiet community that her family had moved to.
Kaitlan Kershner stated she just bought the house at 3650 Lionel Road; her dad lives right beside her and her sister lives right in front of her; she does not want to deal with a gas station on her street that she gets to live on with her son; she worries about traffic, her son and nephew’s safety who live right behind her; they do not want strangers coming up and down Lionel Road; and whatever her sister Brook Moore says that is what she wants to say as well.
James Kershner stated he is probably one of the longest residents on Lionel Road; he has been there since 1976; his parents built the house at 3620, he currently lives at 3630, his daughter just bought the house next door to him, and behind her is Brooke Moore, his other daughter that lives at 3640; he has his own little compound there that he grew up and had his kids go to school at Pinewood; he has seen a lot that goes on, on Lionel Road; it has turned into a drag strip, being a long straight road; with the school being there it was always a concern of his; the residents are all on wells out there in the north end; he talked to the County Sewer Department and they said it is at least $8 to $12 million to run a sewer line up there; and they already have restrictions on the septic tanks, and have septic tanks that need to be redone. He noted with the new systems coming up from a certain area east, he thinks adding a gas station there with the traffic, and kids going in and out of school, his grandchildren in particular, it is not a safe project; he thinks there could be better use for that, more residents, he would love to see more kids move in so his grandchildren have someone to play with after school hours; he is totally against a gas station going in there at the corner of Lionel Road; it is zoned residential; and it does not need to be changed.
Brooke Moore stated she lives at 3640 Lionel Road; her property is within 500 feet of where the suspected gas station is going to go; a couple things she wanted to point out just from stuff that she has researched; within 5.2 miles of her house and where the gas station is wanting to be placed, there are seven gas stations within that radius; she is all for things to come that are going to benefit the community, she just does not think a gas station right there is it; there was a very long discussion the last meeting with the zoning regarding the water quality if a gas station is put in place; and that is ultimately her main concern. She mentioned she does not have an option to get water anywhere else except the ground; having a gas station within 500 feet of her property, the chemicals, the grime, the gas, just from the torrential downpour, everything is going to be seeping into the ground and that is obviously a huge concern for her and her family with the water quality because she does not have any other option; the second thing is definitely the safety; she has lived on Lionel Road for 30 years and she has noticed an increase in crime and traffic; there are cops at the Dollar Store all of the time; there is riff-raff, people riding up and down the road really fast, and when school is in session, between the buses, the after school vehicles, and the cars, everything comes onto Lionel Road; and she does not know what the plan is for how they want to enter if the gas station is put in, but if it is turned onto Lionel Road it is super concerning, especially for the people who live in Quail Haven, because the constant in and out without a light being there. She noted if this was a couple of streets up and the only option for them was to use a well for source, she does not even know if that would be up for discussion because it is her understanding that everything north and east houses cannot be built because of the septic issue right now, everyone wants to protect the Indian River Lagoon; if this is placed there, she asked what happens to that; she went on to say flooding has been a big discussion here in the last five years; the street above her and even to the north, Quail Haven, all of that already floods, so if the gas gets put in, they could put in as many dry ponds but she questions what will happen to those neighborhoods that are directly behind where this gas station is, her and her neighbors to the east; she is not saying that there cannot be some sort of agreement between the owners and the representatives of the property; she is not saying not to build anything at all, she understands they are going to want to sell the property, they have had it for 35 years, and she is sure they want to do something with it, but she just wants to come to some sort of middle ground where it does not have to be a gas station because again she does not have any option where to get her water; and she reiterated that is the biggest concern for her and her family. She commented she walks every day, she will be taking her nephew to school, there are plenty of kids that live on Lionel Road, she grew up walking up and down Lionel Road, playing, and using the public library; and she just does not want that to end because she does not feel safe with the gas station and the Dollar Store going in.
Donna McCone stated she is here to talk about the same project and maybe provide those on the Board who do not know that part of the County as well, what it is like; it is residential with properties, now, mostly more than an acre; it has been rural; when her family came here in the 60’s people did not even want to drive to Mims; there were no traffic lights, or anything; they have seen progress and appreciate the progress, it has happened and it has been good; the people are not saying not to do anything ever, but what they are saying is to abide by the plan that said that Mims says rural; commercial properties were meant to serve the community, not the general public that is going to be going up and down U.S.1; she had no objection to the Family Dollar store, it is the modern version of the corner market; and when there was concern, the company put fresh produce into the market which serves the community. She continued by saying she is very much in favor of things that serve the community, they do not want to be stuck without any public contact; another issue to be addressed beside from the septic which the Board has been hearing a lot about, and the considerable flooding that has been occurring in the neighborhood, the rails to trails culverts need to be redone at the County’s expense, which have not been for years; to approve a project on a property that contains a casement for aquifer on the back side of the property, to approve something that could impact, because the residents are all on wells, they do not have the choice to be on County water; the people feel like this project, one where 60 percent, according to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) figures of gas station underground holding tanks have had at least one leakage issue over their lifetime; imagine the gas leaking into the ground that is going to eventually get to the aquifer and all of the wells in the area being impacted; 60 percent is a big number; and while they are not saying that anybody is going to take any shortcuts, it is just an industry standard that people cannot affect, there is nothing people can do about that, it happens. She commented she hopes the Board will consider this issue in addition to all the other ones that her neighbors have brought up; and she thanked the Board for its time and consideration for the studies done on this property, they were very extensive and the people really appreciate it.
Mickie Reeves stated she lives right down the road from the others and this is the only time they see each other because they live in a rural area, and moved there for that reason; she has lived there for over 40 years, she likes the country, and she likes living in the quiet and peace; Lionel Road has gotten busier and busier; it is not too busy where the residents still cannot enjoy the rural area; she did not like the Dollar Store when it was first coming in, but she will admit she goes there a lot, but there are a lot of police; whatever goes on there she does not know, she visits frequently, but she has not seen any problems; there is a lot of trash coming from there; and it is her understanding that if there is a commercial property zoned, she is still confused as to what they want to put in now; and she knows they are not putting in a gas station, that has been taken away, but once it is changed to commercial, they can basically put in anything they want to, that is her understanding, or what she has been told. She went on to say whatever goes in there, she does not know; they can change it to whatever they want; Pinewood, like has been heard many times, has been there for a long time; she loves it and her children went to school there, her grandbabies go there, it is a great place, and she just likes the kids; she thinks that more commercial property in that particular corner in Mims is the wrong thing to do, especially the traffic; she goes to work in the morning and tomorrow will be the last peaceful day that she will be able to go to work and get there 10 minutes early because school starts; that is okay, but once a commercial building is in there and other things happen, she has no idea what the owner could possibly put in there; the Dollar Store helps the community, the people all go there and purchase things, but they do not know what is going there; it could be a bar, a strip club, she does not know and that is concerning to her, along with Pinewood and there not being any sidewalks there; and the biggest thing is the people all moved there for the rural area, and it is getting more congested with more commercial buildings. She commented he sold the property to the gentleman right side it and she thinks Salib is the same one that sold the guy the property that bought the house that wanted to live in the rural area and now he is selling it and wanting to have commercial property there; and she expressed her appreciation to the Board for listening.
James Bargeron stated he lives on Meadow Green Road a little ways up from here; he hears this stuff, he really does not like it, and this is why he does not like it, they are opposed to the gas station because a person wants to sell their property for maximum profit and potentially gain maximum profit so they can live out their days happy; no problem with that, it is a free enterprise system to make money; that is what it is all about; they come up to the dais and say they do not want a gas station, however, there are only the two, and the two that are local to the area like to price gouge the people first and foremost; secondly, it may create a little bit of competition, drive the price down a little bit in this area, and the one that says specifically, he spends thousands of dollars on tings, he should have opened his pockets a little bit wider and bought the property beside him if he did not like the idea of a gas station; next of all, to face the facts about the guy that said he would support anything but a gas station, that leaves him with pawn shops, liquor stores, crack houses, gun shops, and some many other things, peep shows, just name it; but dang it, they do not want a gas station, which makes absolutely no sense; pick the lesser of the evils, people, it is not hurting anybody; and as far as the undesirables that were talked about, God forbid that some of the teenagers in the area actually have a place to work.
Commissioner Pritchett expressed her appreciation to those who came out to communicate with the Board; and she mentioned the applicant is wanting to zone a BU-1, and inquired what type of businesses can go on in a BU-1.
Bully Prasad, Planning and Development Director, explained typical businesses in a BU-1 include things like a hobby shop, convenience stores, cafeterias, barber shops, bed and breakfast, automobile washing, bait and tackle shops, and things of that nature; and he understands the applicant is looking to restrict certain uses, the more restrictive uses out of that.
Commissioner Pritchett stated there are a lot of BU-2’s but he went with BU-1, which is a little bit better.
Mr. Prasad noted it is less intense.
Commissioner Pritchett stated she is really glad that he is not doing the gas station, and the only reason is, she thinks they are good businesses, but she is concerned about the water situation up in Mims as well; she would love to be able to get full water and sewer out there, but there is going to have to be a lot more businesses and residents come to be able to afford all those connection lines; there is a lot of community commercial already surrounding this area; it is on U.S. 1, so some type of small business up there that helps serve the community does fit; for the Board to consider this, she likes that the applicant is going with a BU-1 and not a BU-2, because there are BU-2’s all over the place; it is less and makes the business a little bit smaller; and she thinks the Binding Development Plan will have to be in place, if the applicant is agreeable to it, she likes that there is consideration for a natural buffer, but she really wants him to leave that whole buffer alone so it stays intact, as it is a nice vegetative buffer and it is already grown up so it gives a little more restriction as far as complicating the neighbors; and she thinks he is putting the pond on that side that the neighbors are next to as well, and she asked if that is correct.
Mr. Ferraro replied affirmatively.
Commissioner Pritchett noted that is going to make it a nice buffer into the north; her other request is that it exit into to business only on and off of U.S. 1; it is already busy and there are a lot of businesses going up and down here; if he does that, she thinks he could make this a very nice business for the neighbors; and she would really like if he could to restrict the access on Lionel Road, so the residents are not impacted in those neighborhoods.
Mr. Ferraro stated he thinks it makes sense to have the in and out access on U.S. 1; they will have to comply with whatever; he does not know if Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) gets involved…
Commissioner Pritchett informed that the applicant has a lot of work, a lot of hoops to jump through.
Mr. Ferraro stated whatever they have to do they can definitely locate the access on U.S. 1.
Commissioner Pritchett stated the area up there is having a lot more problems with water runoff; they have been having that for the last few years; she knows when they do this, Natural Resources Management is going to make them build something to contain their own water runoff, so that is actually going to help a lot of the flooding situations in the area.
Mr. Ferraro interjected by saying vacant properties flood because the natural topography and everything, but a site plan developer engineer will contain all of its water.
Commissioner Pritchett noted they are going to make them do a little extra which is another bonus when they do this; and if the applicant is willing to do this with a BDP, she is willing to go ahead and approve this, as long as in the BDP they are not putting in a gas station right now because she thinks it is a little bit of an underground water situation.
Mr. Ferraro advised it has been added to the restricted use, so there will be no gas station.
Commissioner Adkinson stated the neighbor to the east bought his property next to AU and now there is talk about changing it; she asked if there is anything that can be done to help him not be so uncomfortable with having a 50-foot buffer and lights from a commercial property; can the buffer be made larger; or can anything be done to help as he bought next to AU property.
Mr. Ferraro replied the natural layout of that property when looking at those three lots, the actual building in the back, it is not going to be a huge building because they have already carved out the frontage to be the majority of the corner site and then the site directly to the north; there could be maybe some restriction as to the size of the building if they need to get into that; he cannot imagine it would be more than 5,000 square feet; it is going to be conducive to a campus style retail, professional service type businesses, the dog groomer, the barbershop, the hair salon, CPA office, different types of uses that would serve the community; they also, and he cannot say it will happen, but there have been some conversations with urgent care facility developers that look at that area and might be interested in doing some type of an urgent care facility, however he does not know if that is permitted under zoning or not; but they could limit that.
Commissioner Adkinson noted her question is if a 50-foot buffer is enough to make sure that this gentleman does not have to deal with lights and she is asking if they can do anything for him.
Mr. Ferraro stated 50 feet is a lot.
Commissioner Pritchett commented they are going to put a pond in too so it is actually going to be bigger than 50.
Commissioner Adkinson asked if it is on the east side.
Commissioner Pritchett replied affirmatively.
Mr. Ferraro responded affirmatively as well.
Commissioner Pritchett stated maybe if they are going to do signage to keep it as close as they can to the road so it does not disturb.
Mr. Ferraro replied signage would do no value to anybody in the back, they could make sure all signage is along U.S. 1; and there was also some question about lighting, and there will be no lighting in the back of the property, only lighting around the buildings.
Commissioner Feltner stated he thinks he heard mention of a BDP; one of the things that was done on a property in his District, kind of a similar situation, U.S.1 and close to Post, he is one of those people affected by noise, so he is very empathetic towards neighbors and noise; he aspires to live in a place like what those people have where it is quiet; to that end, the Board had put something in place where there would not be commercial deliveries after 9:00 p.m. and not before 6:00 a.m.; and he inquired if that is something they could do.
Mr. Ferraro answered that is very reasonable.
Commissioner Feltner explained when talking about these other businesses, he thinks he is now understanding it as a strip mall; and he asked if that is fair, there is going to be a six unit strip mall.
Mr. Ferraro replied not a strip mall, separate buildings, three separate small buildings on each lot.
Commissioner Feltner responded they will have two or three dumpsters behind it.
Mr. Ferraro replied potentially there could be a dumpster behind each building.
Commissioner Feltner stated if it is a commercial business they will have delivery trucks come and those kinds of things; it is not lost on him that this is a quiet neighborhood out there; and he does not want to introduce more noise to it.
Mr. Ferraro advised that is reasonable and he will place that in the BDP.
Commissioner Pritchett asked the Clerk’s Office if they have everything that the Board wants to put in the BDP.
The clerk responded affirmatively.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing on a request by Anthony Falanga for a change of zoning classification from AU to RR-1, application number 26Z00017, located in District 2.
Trina Gilliam, Planning and Zoning Manager, stated Anthony Falanga requests a change of zoning classification from AU to RR-1 under application number 26Z00017, located in District 2.
Anthony Falanga stated he is looking to get a rural residential zoning on a two-acre parcel in North Merritt Island that is no longer conforming; it does not meet the minimum acreage requirement; in order to have agricultural property, it has to be two and one-half; quick history, the house directly in front of the two-acre parcel he built with his girlfriend; what they did because they wanted their privacy was purchased the surrounding properties which includes the one in question; unfortunately, the month before they received the Certificate of Occupancy (CO) to move into that house, he lost her to cancer; he lived in the house for almost a year and he just could not do it, so he sold it; it was the biggest mistake of his life because that was their retirement home; after that he decided he wanted to move back and went to the County to find out about getting a permit for that property; and when he first went to the County they had recommended because he did have access from Courtenay Parkway to the property, unfortunately, somewhere in that time frame his mother got Alzheimer's and Policy changed. He went on to say when Policy changed he went back and was politely told that he could still try for the variance but would most likely not get approved; he asked what he should do, and it was suggested that he get that property conforming, rezone it to rural residential; that is what he is here for today; that is the first step to hopefully getting the access from Courtenay Parkway to the property so he can get a building permit; with that said the road that the property is on is called Carew Place; Carew Place at one time had access; it is a private road but it had access and from what he understands was permissible; but when the nursery, the AG user sold the property he thinks it was broken into three parcels and gave it to his family; and that is when it was made non-conforming. He noted there was still access to the property on the road that was there, however he was told by the County, and he went all the way back to microfische and they were wonderful every step of the way, but they looked and looked to try to find access so he did not have to go from Courtenay; basically it was determined that over the years things fell through the cracks and there are way too many easements on Carew Place to allow it to handle another building permit; as far as he knows right now, that is his option; that is why he is here; and he is hoping to get the property zoned from agricultural to rural residential so he can come back across his other piece of property and get access to the rural residential for a building permit.
Rose Plummer stated she is representing the North Merritt Island (NMI) Home Owners Association (HOA); with respect to the request 26Z00017, the NMI HOA Board does not oppose the proposed zoning change from AU to RR-1; and the requested RR-1 zoning designation is consistent with the existing character, pattern, and surrounding land uses in the area and therefore, does not raise compatibility issues or precedent concerns identified previously.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board approved the change of zoning classification from AU to RR-1, application number 26Z00017, tax account 2316489, located in District 2, as requested by Anthony Falaga.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing on a request by BT Rodes, LLC - Padgett Properties Trust, represented by Kelly Delmonico, for a Small Scale Comprehensive Plan amendment, 26S.06, to change the Future Land Use designation from RES 6 to CC, application number 26SS00006, tax accounts 2800696 and 2800697, located in District 5.
Trina Gilliam, Planning and Zoning Manager, stated Items H.7. and H.8., she will read into the record together, however, they will need a separate motion; BT Rodes, LLC, being represented by Kelly Delmonico, requests a Small Scale Comprehensive Plan amendment under 26S.06 to change the Future Land Use designation from RES 6 to CC under application 26SS00006, located in District 5; Item H.8., BT Rodes, LLC requests a change of zoning classification from BU-1-A and AU to BU-2 under application 26Z00020, located in District 5; Planning and Zoning recommended approval with a Binding Development Plan (BDP) limiting the uses to those listed in the applicant’s handout, at the day of the meeting, which included all permitted with conditions and conditional uses under the BU-1 zoning classification, shall be retained together with the selected, permitted, and permitted with conditioned uses in BU-2 zoning classifications, which are permitted uses: dry cleaning and laundry pick up stations, feed and hay for animals and livestock, glass installation, plumbing and electrical shops, testing laboratories, welding repair, and wholesale sales rooms and storage rooms; and uses permitted with conditions include building materials and supplies, commercial entertainment and amusement enterprises, small scale contractors, offices, plants, and storage yards, existing business proposed for expansion, that is the use the applicant is using, garage and mechanical services, service stations for automotive vehicles, and U-Haul services and warehouses.
Kelly Delmonico stated she is the planning consultant on behalf of the property owners; in this case, there are two; she is joined by Jason Bartlett who is with Building Management Systems (BMS), who comes into play with this request; there are two properties being talked about today; the one on the north side of the image that is being looked at is where the location of Building Management Systems has been since 1984; that is 42 years they have been there; she picked this imagine because it shows that communications tower that is right in the middle of the property; it is a little less than an acre, and the established home of BMS; and they are a local general contractor, design, build, and construction manage company and they have just out grown their property. She went on to say that brings in that second piece to the south which is hard to tell with that light that is there; it us a single family property; it is zoned AU, it is larger and mostly clear cut over the years; that has been purchased it is 1.93 acres and that has been purchased in hopes of providing land to expand and support BMS; the idea is that BMS can expand in the future, the business they have now, and also potentially provide units or building space for other types of similar uses in the area that might be spinoffs of that; the primary objective is to align BMS’s current use and their functional use with their Future Land Use and there is zoning; right now that north property is a split zoning; it is zoned BU-1-A which is basically for professional offices, very low intensity uses; almost nothing that BMS has been doing here since 1942 is allowed in that zoning district; therefore, the objective here is to bring that property in line with its functional use, as well as the property to the south so they can continue to expand. She mentioned is they were to step out and look at this area larger, it is a transitioning area; there is single-family around it; there is high density residential to the west, as one can kind of see the apartments there on the west hand side, and then it goes south down the John Rodes corridor to where it is all commercial along 192; the two requests are to change the Future Land Use from Residential 6 which is not compatible with the BU-1-A, so they would go from RES 6 to CC on both properties; and then from BU-1-A, which is the north piece, and AU to BU-2 on that south piece. She noted what she handed out to the Board is the same thing that was presented to the Planning and Zoning Board; it gets into things they are not trying to accomplish there in the red, but in the green are the things the applicant would like to be considered in the future for this business as well as any other business that might co-locate in a unit in the future here; she would be happy to answer any questions on that; she believes that it is consistent with the Future Land Use; it is in an area that is transitioning from single and multifamily to the commercial corridors along John Rodes and 192; it is adjacent to the multifamily, high density residential developments, and the Comprehensive Plan encourages the retention and expansion of local business; and by allowing them to stay here and expand, it secures additional local jobs and maintains a service provider that contributes to the tax base. She stated they have done significant community outreach in this case because they are very aware that they are adjacent to single family residential; the owners went door-to-door knocking on everyone to the north, east, and south that is touching their properties; they spoke to several of the residents and the property owners; the issues that were raised during that door knocking session was they did not want this to be multifamily, and they wanted some type of opaque wall or fence and trees to separate the uses, which would be required to happen anyway, so they are happy to do those; then a community engagement meeting was held on June 2, and she sent out notices to everyone within 500 feet; they only had one attendee, Mr. Carr who lives just to the north, but once he realized no one else showed up, he was fine; and he left as well. She went on to say she has not had any other contact with property owners; the applicants believe that the proposed amendment is a logical correction of the Future Land Use Map (FLUM) to continue to support this business, and it acknowledges the presence of BMS for the last 42 years as a successful contractor’s office in storage; this eliminates logistical hurdles of the split zoning that is there today and provides a clear path for a local business to grow; and with that she is happy to answer any questions.
Chair Altman stated he has a question, he was briefed by staff of this structure to the south of the BMS, and he inquired if that is a home.
Ms. Delmonico replied it is a single-family home.
Chair Altman asked if that is part of the applicant’s request.
Ms. Delmonico answered they are covering both properties so both properties need a new Future Land Use designation.
Chair Altman asked if the intent is to tear that down.
Ms. Delmonico replied affirmatively.
Chair Altman stated across the street looks like a hotel, he has been out there many times.
Ms. Delmonico advised him it is apartments, 300-plus units is her belief; and it is located in West Melbourne.
Chair Altman commented he knows the area well; and he would recommend approval.
Commissioner Pritchett stated the Commissioners up here are very smart; she does with the Commissioner whose District it is in; she never does this but she wants to say one thing, it is very interesting that they put in they are not going to do a seafood processing plant; and that would be horrible.
Ms. Delmonico stated she thought about what in there she would hate to live next to and that was on the top of her list.
Commissioner Pritchett stated she just wanted to make that comment but she is with the Chair in whatever he wants to do.
Chair Altman stated this used to be Doug Padgett’s.
Ms. Delmonico advised it still is.
Chair Altman repeated it still is; and he noted he did not hear the name and that he has known him a long time. He mentioned Mr. Padgett’s dad was his elementary school principal; that is not why he is voting for it; it is a very good request; this business has a great track record and a beautiful place of business; he thinks they are the only applicant that has walked the neighborhood and had neighborhood meetings; he thinks that is fantastic; and he reiterated he thinks it is a very good request.
There being no comments or objections, the Board adopted Ordinance No. 26-14, setting forth the sixth Small Scale Comprehensive Plan Amendment of 2026, 26S.06, to change the Future Land Use Map of the Comprehensive Plan, specifically amending Section 62-501, Part XVI(E), the Future Land Use Appendix and provisions which require amendment to maintain internal consistency with these amendments; providing a legal status; providing a severability clause; and providing an effective date.

action_text:

Mr. Prasad asked for clarification that the motion includes the Binding Development Plan (BDP) as outlined in the applicant’s handout.
Chair Altman replied affirmatively.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board approved a change in zoning classification from BU-1-A and AU to BU-2, application number 26Z00020, tax accounts 2800696 and 2800697, located in District 5 as requested by BT Rodes, LLC, Padgett Properties Trust, to include a BDP to restrict the following uses: seafood processing plant, recovered materials processing facility, bottling beverage and ice plants, flea markets, pet kennels and crematoriums, cemeteries and mausoleums, with property owner agreeing to considerations of permitted uses such as dry cleaning and laundry pickup, feed and hay for animals and stock, glass installations, plumbing and electrical shop, testing laboratories, welding repairs, and wholesale sales rooms and storage rooms, also to include permitted uses with conditions for building materials and supplies, commercial entertainment and amusement enterprises (small scale), contractor’s offices, plants, and storage yards (the business that exists today and wants to expand), garage or mechanical services, service station for automotive vehicles and U-Haul service, and warehouses.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing on a request by Sandman Outdoor Storage, Donald and Stacy Clark, for a change in zoning classification from BU-1 to BU-2, application number 26Z00021, tax account 2000350, located in District 1.
Tina Gilliam, Planning and Zoning Manager, stated this is Sandman Outdoor Storage being represented by Donald and Stacy Clark request a change in zoning classification from BU-1 to BU-2 under application number 26Z00021, located in District 1; Planning and Zoning recommended approval with a Binding Development Plan (BDP) limiting it to all BU-1 uses and retain only BU-2 use for outdoor storage and no Live Local Act.
Donald Clark stated he is seeking a change of use from BU-1 to BU-2 to do outdoor boat and RV storage.
Anthony Fowler stated he is not opposed to the zoning changing from the BU-1 to the BU-2 based on it just being used for the outdoor storage; his concern is that he owns the adjacent 11 acres and has for probably 35 years; when he first bought it, the motel was actually there, but one could not really see it as a vegetative buffer was there; over the years, the vegetative buffer, with Mother Nature taken her toll on that as well as other things happening, which has deteriorated that; in approving this zoning there is going to be more traffic there, more noise there, more headlights, and those types of things; he would like to see a good buffer go back in between their properties that would help with the noise; there is a BU-1 lot and then there is another third adjacent lot that is actually AU, both of which were wooded at one time; the AU lot they are leaving that way for right now, and just asking for this on the BU-1 to go to BU-2; as long as the storage is just going to stay just on the lot that they are applying for and that vegetative buffer, or a good buffer, as sometimes one has to rely on manmade buffers because Mother Nature would take years to put that buffer back in vegetation; and there are some underlying things that he thinks the applicants are working with Code Enforcement and staff with some issues to get to that point to be able to move forward with this and put that vegetative buffer back.
Donna McCone stated she does not have a big problem with the switch from one business to the next in service of the local community; she would really want that BDP to be in place and solid; there is not a great history, and still a pending Code Enforcement issue from 2020; Mr. Clark seems to think that it is better to ask for forgiveness than permission; there are issues with trees gone, things that are still pending; this is 2026 and those items have not been cleared yet; on that property that was for the storage of construction vehicles on the road, the neighbors did not have a problem knowing it was going to be temporary; they even used her street to take those heavy equipment things in and out of that property; now they have asphalt millings there that are covering that area; and she understands that Road and Bridge is going to be issuing a letter within the next few days to a week requiring removal since those are not permitted in residential areas at all and he would need approval for commercial uses. She went on to say those are already there, and the byproducts from that material, again, are seeping into the aquifer; there is just a ton of chemicals in that that are not healthy for people; she appreciates that the property owner wanted to use a permeable substance for that rather than looking at taking away all the drainage, but between the fencing and those things there is some concern in the neighborhood; this is a consensus of 10 neighbors and there are only 10 properties on her street; they have also talked to some people in Quail Haven that are next to it as well; the BDP would need to include that someone would abide by that BDP; and although there are some concerns, there is not a general objection to the change in zoning.
Commissioner Pritchett asked what Ms. McCone would request in the BDP, as she did not interpret that.
Ms. McCone replied that it will only be used as storage, when the property was first acquired by the owners they wanted to do concrete production there which they could actually do now that they have an agreement to be able to do that; she understands that the owner had an auction property and was not happy with the County because they could not do an auction property there; there is a long history; and it is one of contention and acting and then saying maybe they should do something different than what they first wanted to do.
James Bargeron stated he is glad Ms. McCone brought up the millings because he wants to address just that at this point; at the start of this whole situation, a County worker/subcontractor approached Mr. Clark for a place to park equipment and Mr. Clark agreed to the terms to allow them to use his gravel driveway for a parking area, and in return, they offered to bring in millings to stabilize the driveway and parking areas where the equipment could be stored; the worker did not mention permeation or the need thereof; this worker entered into a binding agreement solidifying the verbal contract upon the use of this leased, owned, or subcontracted equipment to deliver, spread, level, aforementioned materials; the County benefited vicariously through the contractors actions by being able to save money, subcontractors, fuel, transport, and other costs and expenditures related to moving and storing the equipment; not only that, there is a working motel on the property that has 24-hour on site security provided by Mr. Clark that the contractor and the County has benefited from and did not incur any subsequent charges for; and this puts the County in a position of both promissory and equitable estoppel. He went on to say the County has received unjust enrichment at Mr. Clark’s expense and therefore, he should be granted a part performance estoppel to stop any further action, because backing out of this agreement now would reinforce all four circumstances allowing litigation in such a case, including a clear misrepresentation; Mr. Clark’s reasonable reliance on the agreement, detrimental change in position by the County, an exceptional injustice including detriment to Mr. Clark’s property and finances; and only one of these criteria is needed proven for litigation, all four verifiable. He continued by saying estoppel being an agreement that one party benefits from but then does not fulfill their end of the agreement; with that said, a worker/subcontractor entered into use agreement is by law, held to the binds of that agreement, be it written, verbal or further; if the subcontractor acting on behalf of the State, misrepresented or misled Mr. Clark with agreements that they were not authorized to make, any remediation is to be sought from the party who misrepresented themselves as able to enter into such agreement; potential remedies to this situation include a variance allowing Mr. Clark to keep the modifications to the property either free of charge or cost of post issued permit; number two, the County send out equipment and a truck at their cost to remove the materials and put Mr. Clark’s land back to the same status it was found in and repay Mr. Clark for all costs and expenditures incurred due to the County’s misrepresentation and pay the owed storage and security charges in the maximum State-allowed charge of $400 per piece of equipment per month stored, as well as the maximum State-allowed fees of late fees for 20 percent per piece per month late from the date of the start of the storage; and additional changes Mr. Clark is entitled to include loss of use for the duration of the storage and the maximum State per day rate for 24-hour unarmed security, not to exceed $960 per law, the stabilizing of the parking lot by the way of milling was used over an existing gravel dirt parking area, which already had road access in two locations, so new road access does not apply, no further road access was created, and millings unlike concrete are permeated so they are not going to keep water laying on them and flooding and all that kind of stuff, it will seep through them. He stated as far as the pollutants that was brought up, there are exactly 1,177 miles of road in Brevard County and if the Board knows what he knows, that takes over 4.7 million tons of asphalt to cover and if this little bit of asphalt he has was a problem in his driveway, it was darn sure a problem in that road and that means Brevard County has a lot of cleanup to do; with that being said, there is no danger from this, otherwise Brevard County would not be selling these millings to landscaping companies that then in turn are allowed to sell them back to other people once they have the permit; and this was a cash grab is what it is.
Carmine Ferraro stated he is just there to support the applicant for approval of his use.
Commissioner Pritchett asked if he is just going to put storage on the property; and if he is good with agreeing to a BDP to just put the storage on there.
Mr. Clark replied he does not know what that is, but sure; he inquired if that is a Binding Development Plan; and he advised he will only be doing boat and RV storage.
Commissioner Pritchett stated she remembers seeing that building since she was a little girl and she is old, so that building has been there for a long time.
Mr. Clark stated he would like to talk for a second about letting P and S Paving use his property for paving U.S. 1 for Brevard County…
Morris Richardson, County Attorney, advised that is the subject of a Code Enforcement case and this is not really the forum; and it is also Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) and the State of Florida, not Brevard County, to be clear.
Mr. Clark asked how he is to get a variance.
Commissioner Pritchett instructed him to call her office and she will see if she can hook him up with the right people to help him with that.
Mr. Clark stated that would be great.
Commissioner Pritchett stated she will copy his card and have someone call him.
Commissioner Feltner stated Commissioner Pritchett might have to say what the BDP is.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board approved the request for a change of zoning classification from BU-1 to BU-2, with a BDP to limit use to outdoor boat and RV storage, application number 26Z00021, tax account 2000350, as requested by Sandman Outdoor Storage.

title: Jeanne A. Benson & Arthur W. Berger Jr. Trust (John Campbell) request a change of zoning classification from AU to BU-2. (26Z00022) (Tax Account 2316445) (District 2) - THE APPLICATION WAS WITHDRAWN BY THE APPLICANT AT THE JULY 13, 2026, PLANNING AND ZONING MEETING.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing as requested by ABRS, LLC for a change of zoning classification from BU-1 to BU-2, application number 26Z00024, tax account 3033535, located in District 2.
Trina Gilliam, Planning and Zoning Manager, stated HBRS, LLC being represented by Landon Scheer, requests a zoning classification change from BU-1 to BU-2 under application number 26Z00024, located in District 2.
Landon Scheer stated this is a unique rezoning request for them in the aspect that the mini-storage as proposed has already been submitted under a site plan application 26SP00014, and it has already gone through one round of DRM comments; they are requesting this rezoning solely for a building material change; ministorage is allowed in BU-1 and also in BU-2, metal buildings are allowed in BU-1 and BU-2, but County Code prohibits mini storages in BU-1 to be metal buildings; this proposed mini storage is just non climate controlled eight feet tall, no utilities, just roll up door, mini storage; and really the industry standard for these are metal buildings. He went on to say that is the request, to change from BU-1 to BU-2 so the applicant can construct these out of metal buildings instead of CMU block infrastructure; it is an allowable use in both zonings; and they have already submitted the site plan for it.
John Hopengarten stated he rises in opposition to this development; he is not a nimby, he is just concerned with too many storage spaces being placed in Brevard County; ministorage is kind of a funny thing, it does not provide any jobs, it does not raise taxes, and it just sits there warehousing personal goods; there are approximately 300 facilities throughout the County; Houston, where he comes from, has only 200 and they have six million people; something is wrong here and the Board should really think this through; putting public storage in Brevard County, this is the Space Coast no the storage coast; this particular facility, like he said previously, will not bring any jobs to the area, it will not give high taxes which are needed right now because the Board is thinking about busting the cap, and there needs to be more tax revenue; and currently in Merritt Island, there are 10 mini storage facilities on that small island. He pointed out that is the map of Merritt Island and those are all the current facilities; putting another one in there to make it 11 is totally unnecessary; there are two just north of the Barge Canal, and this one is further up on Courtenay Parkway, which is proposed; that is the site, it is all trees; there is flooding in that area; if one were to look at the site plan submittal, he is paving the whole entire thing with non-permeable material, where rainwater will not be able to be drained from that site; the other issue that he has is that on one can make a left turn out of that property to go north on Courtenay Parkway; he made an easement request to the Dollar General which is just to the north of that property; and they have granted that. He mentioned, just imagine people coming in through the Dollar General to this property; it is really an issue for the County; think about what the future of this County, is it going to just keep having storage all over the place; he would like to see a moratorium; on Planning and Zoning he has mentioned it many times that there are too many mini storage facilities; the higher and best uses for this property, it is 2.43 acres, they could put affordable housing on there under Live Local, they could do an Assisted Living Facility (ALF), put in an office building, this is the drive to the Space Center, it is right on the curve and people pass it on the way; it just does not seem suitable for this neighborhood, it is all residential, large lots; and he does not believe there is a demand for more and more storage. He stated he would like the Board to consider this and turn this application down as it just does not make sense; as a developer and architect that he is, it is not the highest and best use for this land.
Rose Plummer stated she is there representing the North Merritt Island Homeowners Association (NMIHOA); the NMIHOA has carefully reviewed the zoning change application 26700024 requesting a change in zoning classification from BU-1 to BU-2; after thoughtful consideration of the application, the surrounding land uses, the established character of the corridor, and the interest of the residents and property owners who would be directly affected by this decision, the HOA strongly and respectfully urges the Zoning Board to deny this request; the requested BU-2 classification would significantly broaden the range of potential uses permitted on this property, including more intensive commercial uses that are not compatible with the existing corridor, the nearby residential community, or the reasonable expectations of surrounding property owners; approving this request would create an unnecessary and avoidable risk of introducing uses that are more disruptive, more intrusive, and less consistent with the established pattern of development in North Merritt Island; and this corridor has not developed as an appropriate location for the expanded and more intensive uses associated with BU-2 zoning. She went on to say the existing BU-1 classification already allows for reasonable commercial activity while maintaining important limits that help protect surrounding neighborhoods and property owners; there has been no demonstrated need to expand the zoning classification to BU-2, and the burden should remain on the applicant to show that such a significant change is necessary, appropriate, and compatible with the surrounding area; and based on the information before the Board, that burden has not been met. She continued by saying the NMIHOA has a long standing history of advocating for responsible land use decisions and protecting existing property owners from unwanted, incompatible, and overly intensive development; zoning changes of this nature should not be treated as routine administrative approvals, they have lasting consequences for traffic, noise, lighting, visual character, public safety, property values, and the overall quality of life for residents who have invested in this community, with the understanding that reasonable land use protections would be maintained; approval of this request would also set a concerning precedent for future zoning requests along the corridor; once a more intensive classification is granted, it becomes increasingly difficult to prevent similar requests from following; the cumulative effect of such decisions can permanently alter the character of an area, undermine prior planning expectations, and erode the protections relied upon by nearby homeowners and property owners; and for these reasons, the NMIHOA respectfully request that this Board give substantial weight to the concerns of the surrounding community and deny this application. She noted the requested change from BU-1 to BU-2 is not in the best interest of NMI, it is not necessary to allow reasonable use of the property, and presents an unacceptable risk of incompatible development in an area that should continue to be protected from more intensive commercial encroachment.
Mr. Scheer stated he would like to clarify a couple of things; the mini storage is allowed in both zonings so he is not really there to debate whether or not the mini storage is going to be developed; there is a significant amount of undeveloped land on the western portion of the site that they will not be touching; there is all wetlands in there; there is a huge buffer; the site is 2.34 acres and the area of development is only about 1.8 acres; it was discussed at the Planning and Zoning Board that they would be completely fine with a BDP that would restrict the only BU-2 use to ministorage, to allow them to use the metal building; and the request today is purely a building material change request. He noted he tried to see if there is a way to do it through variance or waiver, but there is just no process for that; the only way to do it was through a rezoning; and the magnitude of price difference between a traditional CMU versus a metal building for this scenario is about double the cost. He commented that is the request, purely a material change; he knows there was mention of an easement, but that was no request to the property owner, it was mandated by Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT), to Dollar General at the time they developed or had their plans approved; mini storage is historically one of the least, lowest in generating traffic, so he does not think it is going to impact the community all that much; and like he already said, there is a massive vegetative buffer that has to be maintained in place because they cannot touch the wetlands.
Chair Altman commented it was mentioned something that he was going to mention, it was said this was wall-to-wall concrete; and he is looking at the site plan and there is significant green space that they are protecting.
Mr. Scheer responded affirmatively. He noted they did that on purpose because they wanted to keep the buildings as far away from the residents as they could and as close to Courtenay Parkway as possible; they are placing the dry ponds behind it to increase that buffer; there is heavy landscaping at the top of those dry ponds on the residential side; and that wetland line that is there obviously they cannot touch it, or anything beyond that line.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board approved the change of zoning classification from BU-1 to BU-2 with a BDP for all BU-1 uses and limiting BU-2 uses to metal self-storage mini warehouse facility only, for application number 26Z00024, tax account 3033535, located in District 2, as requested by ABRS, LLC.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing on a request by Robin R. and Maxine M. Bland, and Tara Brozman for a change of zoning classification from GU to RR-1, application number 26Z00016, tax account 2407139, located District 1.
Trina Gilliam, Planning and Zoning Manager, stated Robin and Maxine Bland, and Tara Brozman being represented by John Campbell request a zoning classification change from GU to RR-1 under application number 26Z00016, located in District 1.
John Campbell stated he is a land surveyor and in his 56th year of practice in Merritt Island; he is representing Robin Bland on this piece of property, in the western part of the County; its Future Land Use is RES1; the predominance of surrounding zoning that is in the Board’s package, is RR-1; they want to go ahead and move this piece of property out of the GU zoning into RR-1, with a provision that they would only want two building sites out of it; it is pretty clear and easy to do; and he has some good clients who want to build their homes on these properties. He mentioned one property would be two acres and one would be a little less than 2.5 acres; he believes the site itself is presently 4.5 acres which is nonconforming even with the GU zoning on it; and he would respectfully ask for the Board to approve the application so they can move ahead; they will be talking with Paul Bodie again because one of the lots is going to be served by a flag lot and they will have to go in for flag lot approval, but they need to get zoning first; and if the Board has any questions he would be happy to answer them.
Commissioner Pritchett commented she was sorry Mr. Campbell had to wait all evening, this was one of the easiest ones all night; and she advised she is going to make a motion to approve it.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board approve the change of zoning classification from GU to RR-1, application number 26Z00016, located in District 1, as requested by Robin R. and Maxine M. Bland, and Tara Brozman.

D.2.

action_text:
Chair Altman called for a public hearing to accept public comments concerning the tentatively adopted County operating and capital budget for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-2027.
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, stated Item D.2. allows for the public to comment on the revised tentative County budget for FY 2026-2027; and before beginning public comment, he would ask the Budget Office to read into the record the revised tentative budget information.
Keith Neterer, Budget Office Director, stated the FY 2026-2027 budget is $2,425,838,420; this budget represents a decrease of $161,915,446, or 6.26 percent less than the FY 2025-2026 current budget of $2,587,753,866.
Mr. Liesenfelt noted staff is now ready to set public comments on the revised tentative budget for FY 2026-2027.
Richard Heffelfinger commented he is going to make his final plea to try to help control some of the costs for Brevard’s citizens; he believes that designating the animal facility is not a critical need or an emergency; he would like to ask the Board to remove $5 million designated for that from the increase over the proposed millage to the General Fund; the reason he says it is not critical is it is an animal care facility; and there currently is one, yet it is 30 years old, he realizes that, but he does not see that meeting the requirements of a critical or emergency need. He stated he also believes the animal care facility back then . . . let him see, they had a meeting on, geez when was it, where they had a budget adjustment, a third-quarter budget adjustment, and it was identified where the County actually saw some General Fund savings, he should not say savings, they were increases due to funds interest, and the Board applied them at that time towards some of the stuff that was identified as critical need in the workshop; there was also one that identified almost $5 million additional increase in what the Sheriff had in his 410 fund Multiple Service Taxing Unit (MSTU); that has been added to proposed budget, it shows he has a carry forward now of almost $8 million; and it shows that only about half of that was allocated, so there is this almost that animal shelter funding in that MSTU fund that is not being expended this year. He pointed out if it is a critical need in an emergency, and since animal care facility falls under the Sheriff, he believes the Sheriff could go back and allocate that money; both things could be gotten and reduce the cost in the General Fund to the taxpayers; that is what he would like to see happen, a motion to remove the $5 million, and then maybe a recommendation to the Sheriff; he does not know who allocates his budget, how those decisions are made; and he knows the County gives it to the Sheriff, but he would like to see him say that is a priority or critical for him since it is under his funding, and move some of that money that he does have.
Dalton Simpson stated he is coming here to speak to the Board about the Stradley Baseball Fields in Cocoa; recently, a few pictures and stuff has been brought to his concern where the sod, the flooding, and baseball season, if it has not already started, it is about to start; right now with the heavy rain, it is starting to cause a lot of flooding, a lot of sod; and he sees that the Board, and he is just starting to get into this, got like a deal with Cocoa, but they are more in supposed to take care of the structures and stuff, and the County is supposed to maintain the fields and the irrigations, any stuff like that. He went on to say he is here to speak about the flooding and ongoing conditions at Stradley Baseball Fields; this is more than wet grass or the field looking bad, this is about a public facility that children, families, coaches, and community are supposed to be able to use safely; when these fields stay flooded, they cannot be maintained properly; practices and games are affected; and the field deteriorate, and it creates safety concerns for the kids using them. He advised what he is asking the County for tonight is simple, they need answers; the residents need to know what is actually causing the flooding, who is responsible for addressing it, and what the plan is to fix it; it is a drainage issue; and he asked if there is a problem with the ditches, covert swells, stormwater system, or the grading of the property. He stated he is sorry, he is nervous.
Chair Altman stated he is doing fine, and while Mr. Dalton finds his way, he has seen pictures of Stradley and it is a mess and a public safety issue; he feels bad for those kids; and he asked the County Manager if he . . .
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, interjected by saying he just has not read it, but he saw part of an email chain going through; the Parks folks have worked with the City of Cocoa on a bunch of issues; and flooding was in there, septic to sewer was in there, and that gentleman right there, Ian Golden, Parks and Recreation Director, if Mr. Dalton would meet with him as soon as he is done speaking, Mr. Golden can give him an update of what is going on.
Mr. Dalton pointed out that would be awesome, he saw Mr. Golden’s name as well; he also sees the County lost a lot of money these past few years on that part of funding; he and his mom played baseball there; his child is young right now; he hears a lot of people talking about it, but that is all they do is talk on the Internet; he wanted to show them this is where he or she comes if they want to see changes, this is where they have to do it; and he found his spot if the Board wants him to finish. He stated whatever the cause is, he is asking for the County to inspect the problem, give the community a clear answer, as their kids deserve a safe, playable baseball field; the coaches and parents who volunteer their time deserve better, and the taxpayers deserve to know that their parks and recreational facilities are being maintained; he is not here tonight just to complain, he is here because he wants to help get something done; and he asked the County to identify the department responsible, which it just did, inspect the flooding and drainage conditions at Stradley Park, and to provide the community with a real plan and timeline for correcting the problem. He noted a lot of people in the community care about these fields and they are paying attention; they just want to see Stradley Park become a safe, usable baseball field for their kids; before he finishes, he wanted to say to rest in peach, Coach Keith Gordon; and his impact on these kids and this baseball community should not be forgotten.
Chair Altman expressed his appreciation to Mr. Dalton for being there; he stated he shares his concerns, and he knows the Commission does as well. He went on to say if there is anything the County can do, he personally feels his pain; he lived through the same thing with his kids when they had mud fields at Viera; now, look at them; they had mud fields in Merritt Island, they have gotten better, so that is needed; this is important to these kids; and he again expressed his appreciation to Mr. Dalton for being there.
Mr. Dalton mentioned he remembers there was a time when Cocoa Little League was a win away from being in the Little League World Series, and they produce a lot of good stuff.
Chair Altman advised this Item needs no vote.
There being no further comments or objections, the Board accepted public comments concerning the tentatively approved budget and millage rates for the County’s 2026-2027 Fiscal Year, including Charter Officers and Dependent Special Districts.
