action_text:
Jim Liesenfelt, County Manager, stated this is what the Board asked staff to bring back at the last Board meeting; staff brought together an Agenda package that shows the different options for the fuel tax which is the one to five local option gas tax and as was mentioned the ninth cent gas tax; it was listed that it could be used for road repaving, resurfacing, drainage, covert replacement, drainage inspection, transit service, traffic operations, transportation construction, capital equipment, and some various other items; attached staff has put together a listing of how each of the counties implement their gas tax; there is a revenue generating option update from Public Works Department; and then there are some questions about electric vehicles, so staff provided some information on what different states do for the registration. He noted last but not least, there is a chart showing how much the gas tax has generated over the past five years; and staff stands ready to answer any questions the Board may have.
Mike Shah, Southeast Petroleum, stated he has lived and done business in Brevard County for more than 46 years; he cares deeply about the future of the community and the Space Coast; he is there to respectfully ask the Board to vote no on any additional local gas tax; he understands the County needs money for roads, drainage, and transportation; these are real needs and they should be addressed; but before adding another tax, one needs to ask what will be the economic consequences and have the propel of Brevard been given a proper voice. He mentioned Brevard County is different than many counties; everyday thousands of people travel into this County to work at the Kennedy Space Center, Cape Canaveral, Defense and Aerospace companies, construction projects, and other businesses; gasoline is a product where the price is displayed in huge numbers, right on the street, and consumers see every penny, just like right now at around $4.17 per gallon of unleaded gas and or $6 for diesel; if the County makes gasoline more expensive in Brevard County people who live or travel out of the County have a choice, some can fill up before entering or after leaving Brevard; when losing that gasoline customer, the business does not just lose gallons, the convenience store can lose the coffee, food, drinks, and other purchases that the customer would have made; and that affects local business independent operators and the employees. He commented if volume declines enough, businesses have to reduce expenses, reduce employee hours, or sometimes reduce their workforce; the County projects that this optional tax could generate approximately $9.1 million per year, but he would respectfully ask does that project fully consider changes in consumer behavior and the potential loss of fuel volume to surrounding counties; before approving this tax, please understand its complete economic impact, not only how much government expects to collect, but what it could cost local businesses and communities; also, most importantly, he believe the tax should have been placed before the voters of Brevard, but having the legal authority to impose a tax and deciding whether public should have a voice are two different questions; is additional transportation funding truly necessary, explain the need to people so they know where the exact money will go, show the project it will fund, and put it on the ballot and let the taxpayers decide; and Brevard County already has a six cent local option tax. He asked the Board to please not solve one problem by creating another problem for the residents, employees, and local businesses; he stated no additional gas tax without the voice of the people, let the voters decide; and he expressed his appreciation to the Board for listening and its service to Brevard County.
Richard Heffelfinger stated he it goes again; there is an opportunity to take some action that has already been offered so many times it is enough to gag a maggot; this was presented to the Board during budget workshops, the exact same numbers were given; now there is a little more information; at least there was some clarification about the electric vehicles because it is only a small percentage of the vehicles using this that would be not being hit; one can play that game about registration he does not care, but here is the thing, Brevard County has a lot of tourists that buy gas in Brevard County; he would rather the tourist pay a little extra and have the residents pay a little extra instead of the Board busting the cap to give $1.6 to road resurfacing; this thing is 8.2, wow that is some good money, the County could actually adjust; the $1.6 does not fix the road resurfacing, the County is billions of dollars in arrears on transportation, but every little bit helps; the County is already taxing the gas, why not just finish it off; there are some good numbers of revenue that comes on the gas taxes; he is seeing $23 million, $25 million, over the years; and this is just another nine and it is a good way to keep it off the backs of the County residents who are paying to make up the difference when there are options, and this is an option. He went on to say what he is saying is he wants the Board to pass tax the gas; he wants everybody in Brevard County to have to pay a little more for gas because he does not want to be paying for it out of his real estate tax; the Board talks about ways and being creative, finding ways to get revenue, and this is one; But the Board has to take the bite; it has been seen over and over again, but the Board refuses to do it; the County already has a whole load of them, and he asked what is one more; he asked the Board to take the bite and take the pressure off the real estate tax because if will not be able to rely on it if that amendment passes; the County is going to be hurting; and the Board better start ponying up. He noted it is going to take courage; he received a compliment from the Chairman about courage to come up and say the Board needs to take some action; there were a lot of things proposed; this was one of them; the Board can do it with a supermajority tonight; he asked them not to kick it down the road, it has been kicked down the road for years; the time to kick has stopped, do it now, get that money for 26/27; take some of the heat; it can re-spread the budgets and take some of that heat off the real estate tax; busting the cap does not look good; this is much easier than busting the cap; and the Board can blame him.
Chair Altman asked if the Board approves this, does it actually develop an ordinance and bring the ordinance back to the Commission for a vote; does the Board need to reach out to the cities; and does that require an interlocal agreement like the original gas tax required; and how that would be divided amongst the cities and the County.
Morris Richardson, County Attorney advised staff would work with the cities on the second local option five cent gas tax, like the first six cents, or there is a default formula that is provided with regard to the ninth cent; and he does not believe there is a municipal share for that, but Ms. Wall knows better than he; in order to levy it however, the County has to levy that by ordinance; there was no direction to have an ordinance today; an ordinance has not been advertised because staff did not have that Board direction; in order to do that to be effective January 1, 2027, it would have to be done by October 1; and the County has to advertise an ordinance for at least 10 days in advance; and the Board would be looking at a special meeting prior to the end of September, if a supermajority vote of the Board wanted to do that. He noted staff would prepare the ordinance and bring it back.
Chair Altman asked so to that point, to advertise an ordinance for consideration, not to pass the local option gas tax, but strictly to advertise the ordinance, does that require a super majority of is passage of the ordinance require super majority.
Attorney Richardson advised technically, a simple majority of the Board could direct him to prepare an ordinance and advertise it and call a special meeting; and as a practical matter, if the votes simply are not there, it may be an exercise in futility, but certainly three Board Members could make that direction and call for the advertisement, schedule the meeting, and all those things.
Chair Altman stated hypothetically staff advertises the ordinance; he wants to be clear, and he asked do they need to reach out to the cities for some sort of agreement or can the Board just pass the ordinance.
Attorney Richardson stated he thinks the ordinance would come first and staff would work with the cities on the agreement; or they could be working that simultaneously if there was clear direction that it was going to implement that.
Commissioner Goodson asked if anybody knows how this will affect construction, diesel, and stuff like that.
Chair Altman commented that is a good question and he asked if diesel is treated differently.
Mr. Liesenfelt state the way he understands it, the one through five would tax diesel; the County is already taxing diesel on the ninth cent; the ninth cent would only put an addition on gasoline.
Commissioner Goodson asked if it is true that even gasoline will affect construction; and does anybody know how much gasoline is bought for construction.
Mr. Liesenfelt responded by saying he does not have that information.
Commissioner Goodson stated he thinks that is something the Board would want to know before voting on this because if it votes on it, and it kills construction, he would find that strange, but maybe everybody else is happy with that.
Chair Altman stated one thing to keep in mind about construction is if the Board were to pass it, all that money would go toward construction, it would produce a significant amount of construction.
Commissioner Goodson commented he is not sure that is because if it goes toward construction and it is forcing people to buy gas to get out to Blue Origin or the Cape, it is going to kill that; and he asked if that is true.
Chair Altman stated he thinks the idea is to provide access to get to Blue Origin, the road is getting pretty crowded; that is probably a discussion and a debate the Board needs to have if it is considering this.
Commissioner Adkinson stated for her, she has talked before about the EV vehicles, but she is also not really very comfortable with the tax right now; everyone keeps saying it is getting difficult out there, so she is not necessarily for a gas tax now, but she is not opposed to placing it on the ballot to let the residents of Brevard County decide; and that is just her two cents.
Chair Altman thanked her for the input.
Commissioner Feltner stated the Board does not have to make the decision now to put something before the voters in 2028; and in fact, the Board can make a decision as late as July 2028 to put something before the voters.
Chair Altman stated that would be the first time this Board would be able to put it before the voters; and he inquired if that is correct, it has to be in a general election.
Attorney Richardson stated the referendum has to be on a general election ballot; the deadline for the November 2028 is going to be sometime in August 2028; and therefore, the Board has a lot of time between now and then, if it wants to go the referendum route, for staff to do an ordinance.
Commissioner Feltner stated the Board can come back after June break and start budget; as part of that it can decide to put this before the voters in 2028; and he is only saying that the Board does not need to take a vote today to put it before the voters in 2028.
Commissioner Pritchett stated she is out of here so she is not going to take any hit on this; she was willing if the Board wants to do it because at that time it is going to be near election time and everybody gets a little more hesitant; it is going to depend on whether anyone is willing to take the hit, which she hopes the Board members are because that is what makes public leadership fun, going ahead and doing what one knows is right…
Commissioner Feltner noted he was just making the distinction.
Commissioner Pritchett continued by saying if the Board is willing to do that, she is impressed.
Chair Altman asked if there needs to be a motion, he does not think there needs to be a motion on the floor.
Attorney Richardson advised this is just bringing back the request for discussion and direction; and he only needs a motion if the Board wishes to give any direction.
Chair Altman asked if there is any motion on this Item and if not he will move on.
The Board discussed but took no action on the consideration of a ninth-cent unleaded motor fuel tax and local option unleaded motor fuel gas tax.

action_text:
Chair Altman stated the Mayor from Pal Bay has very patiently sat through this entire meeting; the Board received a letter and there are a couple of cards; he would like to talk a little bit before hearing the public comment; he received a letter from the City of Palm Bay requesting the Board to consider reaching out to the Central Florida Expressway (CFX) Authority to have them simply conduct a study to do a toll feasibility study to see if Heritage Parkway could be built through as a toll facility; right now there is no money and no way that it is going to be built in any comprehensive way; he has a letter that mimics what the city of Palm Bay requests, very similar, agreeing to that and responding to the City of Palm Bay, and asking for Central Florida Expressway Authority to conduct this study to see if it is possible; and he would like to recognize Mayor Rob Medina.
Rob Medina, Mayor of Palm Bay, stated it has been years since he has been in these chambers; as the Board well knows, he was an aid to a County Commissioner so he feels right at home; he sees the additions of security as these doorways were always accessible, but times have changed; first and foremost, before he asks about any requests, he wants to take the opportunity to thank the Board Members; he understands what it is to serve; he understands the sacrifices; and Commissioner Pritchett nailed it, it is always about doing the right thing, and taking the heat for doing the right thing. He went on to say he is here to support Palm Bay’s venture; the Palm Bay City Council unanimously gave direction to staff to look at additional ways to improve the evacuation corridor which includes the south part, many people understand it as ‘The Compound’; the City has renamed it the Phoenix Business Park; but that is another story. He continued by saying ever since Covid the City’s population has increased and south Brevard continued to increase; the City Council has to look at mobility ranges and different accessibilities; evacuation is critical and part of that is what are people going to do with the south side of the Heritage Parkway to connect onto that 1-95 corridor; his staff has identified and had meetings with Central Florida Expressway; in an opportunity to conduct a feasibility study that would probably cost in the range of $1 million, absolutely free to them; they would like to get that intel to see how, as a body, well informed on how it could move this community forward in regards to the City’s future; if the Board has any questions please ask; this is a letter of support that would come from the County; the Space Coast Transportation Planning Organization (TPO) as the Board is well aware, supported this; and he is just coming to the Board requesting that concurrency and support.
Chair Altman stated he has a question and he thinks he knows the answer but he wants it on the record; and he asked if the $1 million is something the Expressway Authority has agreed to pay for 100 percent.
Mr. Medina replied affirmatively, stating it will not cost the City or the Board; it is exciting that they will conduct a study; public input is part of that; it is exciting that it will not cost the City a cent but it will be able to gather intel and whichever way they go, the information will be readily available to everyone.
Chair Altman stated he has reached out to Expressway Authority to get verification, and he would never doubt Mr. Medina; in the County’s letter he is asking for the feasibility study to be from I-95, exit 166 to I-95 exit 182; that is basically from the Micco interchange and I-95 up to the Ellis Road interchange; they are looking at the whole corridor; and there are a couple cards. He expressed his appreciation to the Mayor.
Mayor Medina expressed his appreciation to the Board.
Richard Heffelfinger stated he is confused about where the Board is talking about putting this; the St. John’s Heritage Parkway starts at 192 and he thinks it runs all the way down to… he asked what road is that, if Ellis Road is included, and if that is County owned or a Palm Bay road.
Chair Altman advised it is multiple jurisdictions; there is an extensive corridor study that was commissioned and completed where it evaluated a potential corridor, but there is no specific corridor; some of it has been completed, but only a two-lane portion of it; some of it has right-of-way acquisition and a lane, others is a big question mark. He noted this is a planning process.
Mr. Heffelfinger inquired if CFX has not been approached about this yet.
Chair Altman replied he has spoken with them, but it has not been formalized in terms of the letter.
Mr. Heffelfinger stated he will bring up another issue, it is kind of procedural thing; and he asked who is Brevard County’s CFX representative to that board.
Chair Altman stated it was Commissioner Delaney, and he is going to address that under his Board report later on in the meeting.
Mr. Heffelfinger replied ok, so he is going to designate a CFX because nobody’s been there since April.
Chair Atman responded in the affirmative.
Mr. Heffelfinger pointed out nobody has been there since April; he was just wondering because this came out of the weeds and the County does not have a representative; and he does not know what is being done here. He noted in the past Commissioner Delaney made statements that people did not want toll roads in this County; they have plans in 2045 to come over with 524; they have multiple corridors which it does solve a lot of problems, the evacuation problem that has been identified multiple times, and when one builds, people still need to get out when there is a hurricane; he thinks this Board may be in violation of some of that requirement from the State; he has heard that, does not know if it is true; he might have read it on the internet, but he knows there is a requirement; that would be great if CFX would just build the road, improve the road, and take tolls and pay for the maintenance; it would be of the table to the County; and he asked if that is true.
Chair Altman stated it is possible if the numbers work.
Mr. Heffelfinger stated if they are collecting tolls he hopes they are paying for the road and all the maintenance too; and that is how it works.
Chair Altman commented it could be 100 percent or it could be partial; and there is precedent throughout Central Florida.
Mr. Heffelfinger stated if they took 100 percent he thinks that would be a good thing because there is no transportation money to pay for that. He commented he just had some questions and he does not know the whole toll thing; but to do a study and they are going to pay for it, he is sure they would love to do the study so they can try to sell the Board a toll road; they need more toll roads because CFX is poor; and that is all he had.
Jason DeLorenzo, Deputy City Manager for the City of Palm Bay, stated when he arrived in Palm Bay about a year and a quarter ago, they started having regular meetings about what they formally called the Compound, now as the Mayor said, the Phoenix Business Park area; those planning sessions have been fruitful; they have brought in almost $6.5 million of State and Federal grants for infrastructure; the one thing they kept bumping up against is how to solve this 13 and one-half mile gap from Malabar Road down to the southern interchange; the estimate is that is going to be between $250 and $400 million to create that with land acquisition and everything else that is going to be needed; and that brainstorming led them to reaching out to the CFX to just have a conversation and understand what they do and how they do it. He mentioned that and some future conversations with County staff and TPO led them to this potential feasibility study as was heard from the Mayor, fully-funded by them to understand the corridor; he likes the Board’s suggestion that it be expanded all the way up to Ellis Road and consider the entire piece which is almost 20 miles worth of road for economic development; of course, the biggest piece is that evacuation route from the southern end of the County up into the Central part of the County; and every time 1-95 gets closed for a bad accident or wildfire, there is all kinds of trouble along Babcock, so they are looking for an alternative corridor to help them through those situations. He mentioned is is just asking for the Board’s assistance with this letter of support; and he will answer any questions if the Board has any.
Chair Altman stated he will bring this back to the Board; he works at the Space Center and it is very difficult now; there are a lot of employees who live in Palm Bay that work in the Space Launch Center, but many are unable to work up there now because it is about a 2-hour drive; people said the hard part is about 45 minutes to an hour of that is just getting out of Palm Bay; it has huge economic impacts on all of the County and the desire to do what it does best, is to put people into space; nobody does that better; there are other reasons in South Brevard that they need to have an ability and this may be the residents only hope; and he would like to ask for support from the rest of the Board to send a letter to CFX.
The Board approved and authorized the Chair to sign the letter of support for a feasibility study for the St. Johns Heritage Parkway.

title: Approval, re: Letter of support for a Facility Feasibility Study for the St. Johns Heritage Parkway
